definition_zh: 高原；台地；平台期；平稳阶段；托盘
definition_en: a large area of high flat land; a period when progress stops rising; a flat tray or dish
core_image: 地面被整体抬高之后，顶部留出一大片几乎水平的平面，边缘却突然下落
scene: 车爬上长坡之后，眼前忽然展开一片望不到边的平地。After the long climb the road crosses a wide plateau.
sceneCN: 此处指「被整体抬升、顶部平坦的大片高地」（第 1 个义项：海拔高而表面近乎水平的大区域）；句意为爬完长坡之后，公路穿过一片宽阔的高原。图中可辨识物件：长坡、水平的地平线、突然下落的边缘、稀疏植被。

pos.zh: 高原；台地；平台期；平稳阶段；托盘
高原的；平台期的（如 plateau phase）

derivatives.zh: 高原（复数）；（他、她、它）趋于平稳
高原（法语式复数）
已进入平台期的
趋于平稳的过程

senses.title: A large high flat area
senses.definition: an extensive area of land raised well above its surroundings and mostly flat on top
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围、顶部大体平坦的大片陆地
senses.example: After the long climb the road crosses a wide plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 爬完长坡之后，公路穿过一片宽阔的高原。
senses.why: French plat meant 'flat', and the diminutive plateau named a flat raised surface; geography kept the flatness and the height.
senses.whyCN: 法语 plat 意为「平的」，指小形式指平坦的抬高面；地理学保留了「平」与「高」两点。

senses.title: A small tableland or mesa
senses.definition: a smaller flat-topped elevated area with steep edges
senses.definitionCN: 边缘陡峭、顶部平坦的较小高地
senses.example: The village sits on a low plateau above the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村子坐落在河上方的一块低台地上。
senses.why: The form comes in sizes: a mesa is the small version of the same flat-topped shape.
senses.whyCN: 这种形状有大小之分：台地就是同一种平顶形状的小型版本。

senses.title: A learning plateau
senses.definition: a stage in learning when improvement seems to stop for a time
senses.definitionCN: 学习中进步暂时看似停止的阶段
senses.example: Most learners hit a plateau after the first few months.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数学习者在最初几个月后都会遇到平台期。
senses.why: A rising curve that turns flat looks like a plateau: progress continues sideways instead of upward.
senses.whyCN: 上升的曲线转为水平，看起来就像高原：进步横向延伸而不再向上。

senses.title: A period of stable performance
senses.titleCN: 表现平稳期；增长停滞期
senses.definition: a period when performance or growth stays level rather than rising
senses.definitionCN: 表现或增长保持水平而不再上升的时期
senses.example: Sales reached a plateau in the second half of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 销量在下半年进入平稳期。
senses.why: Business graphs reuse the landform: a flat stretch between two rises is read as a plateau.
senses.whyCN: 商业图表沿用这个地貌：两段上升之间的平坦段被读成高原。

senses.title: The flat section of a graph
senses.definition: the horizontal portion of a curve where the value does not change
senses.definitionCN: 曲线上数值不变的水平部分
senses.example: The dose-response curve shows a clear plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 剂量反应曲线出现明显的平台段。
senses.why: Mathematics names the horizontal stretch after the shape it resembles.
senses.whyCN: 数学根据所像的形状来命名那段水平区间。

senses.title: A raised flat-top structure
senses.definition: an elevated flat surface in a building, a stage or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、舞台或机器上的抬高平面
senses.example: The stage has a plateau where the chorus stands.
senses.exampleCN: 舞台有一块合唱队站立的平台。
senses.why: The word describes the shape wherever it occurs, not only in geography.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是形状本身，出现在哪里都算，不只用于地理。

senses.title: To level off
senses.definition: to stop rising and stay at the same level
senses.definitionCN: 停止上升并保持在同一水平
senses.example: Demand plateaued after the price increase.
senses.exampleCN: 涨价之后需求趋于平稳。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to plateau is to take on the flatness of the landform.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：这样用就是呈现出这种地貌的平坦。

senses.title: A flat serving tray
senses.definition: a flat dish or tray for carrying or displaying things, especially in French-style use
senses.definitionCN: 用来端送或陈列物品的平盘，尤见于法语风格用法
senses.example: The waiter set the plateau of cheeses on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 侍者把那盘奶酪放到桌上。
senses.why: The oldest French sense was a flat dish; English kept it as a decorative or serving term.
senses.whyCN: 最早的法语义就是平盘；英语把它保留为装饰或端送用的说法。

intro.en: Plateau is a French diminutive of plat 'flat', from Latin plattus, ultimately Greek platys 'broad, flat'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: plateau 是法语 plat「平的」的指小形式，源自拉丁 plattus，最终来自希腊 platys「宽而平」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek platys meant 'broad, flat'; it also underlies platysma and the geological term platform through other routes.
items.cn: 希腊 platys 意为「宽而平」；它也通过其他路径构成 platysma 与地质学术语 platform。

items.en: Latin plattus 'flat, broad' was a colloquial borrowing from Greek and passed into the Romance languages.
items.cn: 拉丁 plattus「平的、宽的」是来自希腊语的口语借词，随后进入罗曼语族。

items.en: French plat meant 'flat' and, as a noun, 'a flat dish'; the diminutive plateau first named a flat tray or platter.
items.cn: 法语 plat 意为「平的」，作名词指「平盘」；指小形式 plateau 最初指平托盘或大盘。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries travellers applied plateau to the flat highlands of interior continents, and the landform sense became dominant.
items.cn: 在 18 与 19 世纪，旅行者把 plateau 用于内陆的平坦高地，地貌义随后占据主导。

items.en: The 'period of no progress' sense is twentieth-century, borrowed from the flat stretch of a graph.
items.cn: 「停滞期」义属于 20 世纪，借自图表上的平坦段。

items.en: The main line is secure; only the first date of each sense is approximate. The pre-Greek origin of platys is not established, so deeper forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 主要线索可靠，只有各义项的首见年代为约数。platys 在希腊语之前的来源尚未确立，更早的形式均属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words that share the plat- shape; the second holds landform words for high flat ground.
note.cn: 第一组是共享 plat- 形状的词；第二组是表示高而平坦地面的地貌词。

entries.definition: A flat dish or a flat sheet of metal; it comes from the same French plat family but has no raised-land sense.
entries.definitionCN: 平盘或金属平板；同出法语 plat 词族，但没有高地的意义。

entries.definition: A large flat dish for serving food; it is a dish word, not a landform word.
entries.definitionCN: 端送食物的大平盘；它是餐具词，不是地貌词。

entries.definition: A small military unit; it comes from French peloton, of different formation, and only looks as if it belongs here.
entries.definitionCN: 小型军事单位；来自法语 peloton，构词不同，只是看起来像同族。

entries.definition: The French-style plural of plateau; it is the same word in another number form.
entries.definitionCN: plateau 的法语式复数；只是同一个词的另一种数的形式。

entries.definition: A broad flat elevated region; the word says plainly what plateau says in French.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔平坦的高地；这个词把 plateau 用法语表达的意思直接说了出来。

entries.definition: A flat-topped hill with steep sides, borrowed from Spanish 'table'; it is smaller than a plateau.
entries.definitionCN: 顶部平坦、侧壁陡峭的小山，借自西班牙语「桌子」；比高原小。

entries.definition: Land that is higher than the surrounding area, without the strong flatness that plateau requires.
entries.definitionCN: 高于周围地区的地面，但不强调 plateau 所要求的平坦。

entries.definition: Elevated country, usually hilly or mountainous; it is high but not necessarily flat.
entries.definitionCN: 抬高的地区，通常多丘或多山；它高，但不一定平。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real French flat word, the real graph metaphor and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的法语「平」词、真实的图表比喻与固定搭配。

normal.en: French plat 'flat' + -eau (diminutive): a flat raised surface.
normal.cn: 法语 plat「平的」+ -eau（指小）：一块抬高的平面。

normal.en: The family runs plateau, plateaus, plateaux, plateaued, plateauing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 plateau、plateaus、plateaux、plateaued、plateauing。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reach a plateau, plateau phase, learning plateau, high plateau.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 reach a plateau、plateau phase、learning plateau、high plateau。

normal.en: The landform and the graph share one shape: rise, flat, rise again.
normal.cn: 地貌与图表共享同一个形状：上升、变平、再上升。

normal.en: A plateau is high and flat; a mesa is the small version; a tableland is the plain English name.
normal.cn: plateau 高而平；mesa 是它的缩小版；tableland 是平实的英语名称。

abstract.en: Picture a table lifted a kilometre into the air, its top still level.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被抬到一千米高空，桌面仍然水平。

abstract.en: Picture a climbing line that suddenly turns sideways and runs flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条上升的线突然转向水平延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a plate held up by a thick stem of rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子被一根粗岩柱托起。

examples.en: The plateau is dry, windy and covered with short grass.
examples.cn: 这片高原干燥、多风，覆盖着矮草。

examples.en: Her running times plateaued after the injury.
examples.cn: 受伤之后，她的跑步成绩趋于平稳。

examples.en: After rapid growth, membership reached a plateau.
examples.cn: 会员人数在快速增长之后进入平台期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「平（pla）+ 托（teau）」—— 被高高托起却依然平的一大块地 → 高原；平台期

root: 法语 plateau（plat「平的」的指小形式）← 拉丁 plattus「平的」← 希腊 platys「宽而平」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same profile: something rises, then runs flat for a long stretch, whether that stretch is land, learning, sales, a graph, a stage or a tray.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一个轮廓：某物升起后在一段很长的距离上保持水平，无论这段是土地、学习、销量、图表、舞台还是托盘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised surface whose top stays level while its edges drop away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被抬高的表面，顶部保持水平，边缘却向下落。

branches.en: THE LAND: a broad high flat area and its smaller flat-topped cousin.
branches.cn: 土地：大片高而平的地区，以及它较小的平顶近亲。

branches.en: THE CURVE: learning, performance and graphs all go flat for a while.
branches.cn: 曲线：学习、表现与图表都会有一段时间走平。

branches.en: THE ACTION: to plateau is to take on that flat profile.
branches.cn: 动作：plateau 作动词就是呈现出这种平坦轮廓。

branches.en: THE BUILT FORM: a stage or platform repeats the shape.
branches.cn: 人造形态：舞台或平台重复了这一形状。

branches.en: THE OLD DISH: the French tray sense survives as a serving word.
branches.cn: 古老的盘子：法语的托盘义作为餐具词保留下来。

intro.en: Plateau is a French diminutive with two accepted plurals; English also made it a verb in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: plateau 是法语指小形式，有两种被接受的复数；英语在 20 世纪还把它用作动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin plattus 'flat' comes from Greek platys 'broad, flat'; the same Greek word underlies plate, platter and the geological platform through separate routes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plattus「平的」来自希腊 platys「宽而平」；同一个希腊词通过不同路径也构成 plate、platter 与地质学术语 platform。

items.example: The plateau stretches for hundreds of kilometres.
items.exampleCN: 这片高原延伸数百公里。

items.meaning: more than one plateau; it levels off
items.example: Two plateaus lie east of the river.

items.meaning: more than one plateau, in French-influenced style

items.example: Plateauing is common after early gains.
items.exampleCN: 早期收益之后出现平台期很常见。

items.example: The drug showed a plateau effect at high doses.
items.exampleCN: 这种药在高剂量时表现出平台效应。

items.meaning: a stage in which values stay level
items.example: The plateau phase lasted two weeks.

items.meaning: a stage where learning slows to a stop
items.example: A learning plateau can be broken by new practice.
items.exampleCN: 换一种练习方式可以打破学习平台期。

items.example: The plate is wider than the tray.

latinEntries.structure: platea, plateae (f., first declension, from Greek plateia)

definition_zh: 站台；平台；政纲；讲台
definition_en: the raised area beside a railway track where passengers get on and off; also a base for services, a set of political aims, or a raised stage
core_image: 一块高出地面的平整台面，四周有人上上下下，台面把人和地面隔开
scene: 清晨的车站人潮涌动，广播反复提醒乘客退到黄线之后。A woman with a heavy suitcase stood on the platform waiting for the slow train.
sceneCN: 这里是「站台、月台」（第 1 个义项）；句意为一位提着沉重行李箱的女士站在站台上等慢车。图中可辨识物件：黄线、铁轨、行李。

derivatives.zh: 由 platform 加 -er 构成，指以跳跃平台为核心玩法的游戏类型
由 platform 加 -ing 构成，指平台跳跃类玩法
由 multi- 与 platform 复合而成，义为「跨平台的」

senses.title: The raised edge beside a railway line
senses.definition: the long raised surface beside the track where people wait for and board trains
senses.definitionCN: 铁轨旁供人候车、上车的长条形高台
senses.example: The train to the airport leaves from platform three.
senses.exampleCN: 去机场的列车从三号站台发车。
senses.why: French plateforme first meant a flat ground plan; applied to stations, the flat raised strip beside the rails kept the same picture of a level surface lifted above the ground.
senses.whyCN: 法语 plateforme 最初指平坦的地面规划；用到车站上，铁轨旁那条高出地面的平条仍保留「一块被抬起的平面」这幅画面。

senses.title: A base on which services or work run
senses.definition: a system, website or piece of equipment that other things are built on or run through
senses.definitionCN: 其他事物赖以建立或运行的系统、网站或设备
senses.example: Small shops sell through a shared online platform.
senses.exampleCN: 小商户通过一个共用的网络平台卖货。
senses.why: The computing sense keeps the physical image: something flat and stable underneath, on which other things stand, except now what stands there is software and trade.
senses.whyCN: 计算机义保留了这个物理画面：底下有一块平整稳固的东西，别的东西站在上面，只是如今站在上面的是软件与生意。

senses.title: A set of political aims
senses.definition: the declared policies and promises on which a party or candidate seeks support
senses.definitionCN: 政党或候选人争取支持时公开宣示的政策与承诺
senses.example: Housing reform was the centrepiece of her platform.
senses.exampleCN: 住房改革是她竞选纲领的核心。
senses.why: A platform is also the flat sheet a plan is drawn on, so a party's written aims are literally the plan it stands on before the public.
senses.whyCN: platform 也指铺开画方案的平面，所以一个政党写下的主张，字面上就是它站在公众面前时脚下的那份方案。

senses.title: A raised stage for speaking
senses.definition: a raised floor from which someone speaks to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 供人向听众讲话的高出地面的台子
senses.example: The speaker climbed the platform and adjusted the microphone.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者登上讲台，调了调话筒。
senses.why: Here the oldest physical picture is visible again: a flat slab lifted so that one voice can be seen and heard above a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这里最古老的物理画面重新出现：一块被抬高的平板，让一个人的声音在人群之上被看见、被听见。

intro.en: Platform is a French compound of flat and form; it named a ground plan before it named any raised surface in English.
intro.cn: platform 是法语中「平坦」与「形状」的复合词；在英语里它先指地面规划图，之后才指各种高出地面的台面。

items.en: Old French plat meant flat, and it goes back to a Vulgar Latin form usually reconstructed as plattus.
items.cn: 古法语 plat 意为平坦的，一般上溯到通俗拉丁语中重构为 plattus 的形式。

items.en: Old French forme meant shape or form, from Latin forma.
items.cn: 古法语 forme 意为形状、形式，来自拉丁语 forma。

items.en: The compound plateforme named a flat diagram or ground plan, a map-like scheme rather than a built thing.
items.cn: 复合词 plateforme 指平面图或地面规划，是图纸式的方案，而非建成的实物。

items.en: English borrowed it as platform, first for a plan or scheme, then for a raised level surface such as a stage.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 platform，先指方案、规划，后指讲台一类的高出地面的平面。

items.en: Railways gave it the station sense, politics gave it the programme sense, and computing gave it the sense of a base for services.
items.cn: 铁路带来站台义，政治带来纲领义，计算机则带来「服务赖以运行的底座」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the French stem for flat and form; the near-meaning group gathers raised surfaces and bases to stand on.
note.cn: 形近组共享法语中「平坦」与「形状」的词干；近义组收表示高台与落脚基座的词。

entries.definition: A wide area of high flat land.
entries.definitionCN: 高原；大片高地。

entries.definition: A flat dish, or a flat sheet of metal.
entries.definitionCN: 盘子；平板。

entries.definition: A remark so flat and ordinary that it says nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无味的套话。

entries.definition: A game built around jumping between platforms.
entries.definitionCN: 以在平台间跳跃为核心的游戏。

entries.definition: A raised floor where performers appear.
entries.definitionCN: 供表演者登台的高出地面的台子。

entries.definition: A small raised stand for a speaker or conductor.
entries.definitionCN: 供演讲者或指挥站的小高台。

entries.definition: A place or setting where public discussion happens.
entries.definitionCN: 进行公开讨论的场所或场合。

entries.definition: The lowest part on which something rests.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所依托的底部。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the idea of flat with the idea of shape, and every sense is still some flat surface that other things stand on.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把「平坦」与「形状」合在一起，而每个义项至今仍是某块供别的东西站立的平面。

normal.en: Plateforme joins plat, flat, with forme, shape: a flat shape.
normal.cn: plateforme 把表示平坦的 plat 与表示形状的 forme 合起来，就是「一个平的形状」。

normal.en: A station platform is literally a flat form raised beside the track.
normal.cn: 车站站台字面上就是铁轨旁被抬起的一块平形。

normal.en: A political platform is a flat plan laid out for voters to read.
normal.cn: 政治纲领就是摊平铺开、让选民看清楚的一份计划。

normal.en: A digital platform is the flat base that apps stand on, the old physical image moved into software.
normal.cn: 数字平台就是应用所站立的平整底座，旧的物理画面被搬进了软件。

normal.en: Platformer adds -er to name the kind of game that is all about platforms.
normal.cn: platformer 加 -er，用来命名那种全靠平台跳跃的游戏。

abstract.en: A word for a flat plan became a word for a place to stand: in English, planning and standing keep sharing one surface.
abstract.cn: 一个表示平面图的词变成了表示落脚处的词：在英语里，规划与站立始终共用同一块平面。

abstract.en: Every platform is a small act of separation, lifting people a step above the ground they came from.
abstract.cn: 每个平台都是一种小小的分离，把人从原来的地面上抬起一步。

abstract.en: When a party calls its aims a platform, it is saying that words should be something people can stand on.
abstract.cn: 当一个政党把主张称作 platform，它是在说：言语应当成为人们可以站上去的东西。

examples.en: The express to the coast leaves from platform six.
examples.cn: 开往海岸的快车从六号站台发车。

examples.en: The company built a platform where farmers can sell directly.
examples.cn: 这家公司搭建了一个让农户直接销售的平台。

examples.en: Both candidates published their platforms before the debate.
examples.cn: 两位候选人都在辩论前公布了竞选纲领。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来特福姆」——火车扑过来之前，人先站上那块平平的台子。

root: 古法语 plat（平坦，一般上溯通俗拉丁语 plattus）+ forme（形状，来自拉丁语 forma）→ plateforme → 英语 platform。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a flat surface raised for use; the senses split into the station edge, the base for services, the political plan and the speaker's stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块为使用而抬高的平面；义项分化为车站边沿、服务底座、政治纲领与演讲台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat slab lifted above the ground, with people stepping on and off it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块高出地面的平整台板，人们在其上上下下。

branches.en: a yellow line and a waiting crowd beside the rails

definition_zh: 请；使高兴；使满意；随自己的意愿
definition_en: used as a courteous word when asking for something, or to give someone satisfaction
core_image: 菜单被轻轻推到你面前，对方退后半步，等你先开口
scene: 餐厅里，服务员把菜单轻轻推到你面前，退后一步等你点单。Please take your time; the waiter will come back in a moment.
sceneCN: 这里用的是「请」这一客套说法（第 1 个义项：礼貌地提出请求或邀请）；句意为请慢慢看，服务员稍后再过来。画面里有餐桌、菜单和退到一旁等候的服务员。

pos.zh: 使高兴；使满意；随自己的意愿

derivatives.zh: 由 please 加后缀 -ed 构成，表示「感到高兴的；满意的」
由 please 加后缀 -ing 构成，表示「令人愉快的；讨人喜欢的」
经古法语 plaisant 进入英语，与 please 同源，义为「令人愉快的；宜人的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 please 构成，义为「使不快；惹恼」
由 pleasing 加 -ly 构成，义为「令人愉快地」

senses.title: A courteous word in a request
senses.definition: used when asking for something or inviting someone to act, so that the request sounds polite
senses.definitionCN: 在提出请求或邀请别人做某事时使用，使语气显得客气
senses.example: Please close the window before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 走之前请把窗户关好。
senses.why: The verb first meant to be agreeable to someone, and the request use keeps that attitude: the speaker puts the other person's comfort first and asks softly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的动词本义是「令某人觉得合意」，请求用法延续的正是这种姿态：说话人先把对方的舒适放在前面，于是请求变得轻而客气。

senses.title: To give someone satisfaction
senses.definition: to make someone feel happy, content or satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 让某人感到高兴、满意或称心
senses.example: The simple answer seemed to please the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个简洁的答复似乎让整个委员会都很满意。
senses.why: Latin placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to a person, so the one who is pleased is always the judge of whether the action worked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 placere 意为「令人觉得合意、可接受」，所以被取悦的那个人始终是判断这件事成不成的人。

senses.title: To do as one wishes
senses.titleCN: 随自己的意愿；自行其便
senses.definition: to act according to your own wish rather than someone else's, as in the phrase please yourself
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的想法行事而不迁就别人，常见于 please yourself 这一说法
senses.example: You can please yourself about the seating arrangement.
senses.exampleCN: 座位怎么安排，你随自己的意思就好。
senses.why: If pleasing means making a person content, then pleasing oneself turns that contentment inward: the same verb now names a choice made for the speaker alone.
senses.whyCN: 既然 please 是「让人称心」，那么 please oneself 就是把这份称心转向自己：同一个动词在此指只为说话人自己作的选择。

intro.en: Please goes back to a Latin verb meaning to be agreeable, travelled through French, and in English shrank into the small polite word used in requests.
intro.cn: please 源自一个表示「令人觉得合意」的拉丁动词，经法语传入英语，最后又缩略成请求句里那个轻巧的客套词。

items.en: Placere meant to be pleasing or acceptable to someone, and it could describe a person as well as a thing.
items.cn: placere 意为令某人觉得愉快、可以接受，既可以形容事物，也可以形容人。

items.en: The related noun placitum named what seemed good and therefore a decision; it fed plea and plead rather than the verb please itself.
items.cn: 相关的名词 placitum 指「看起来好的事」，引申为决定；它后来生出 plea 与 plead，而不是动词 please 本身。

items.en: Old French used plaisir both as a verb meaning to please and as a noun for the pleasure that followed.
items.cn: 古法语中 plaisir 既是动词「使高兴」，也是名词「随之而来的快乐」。

items.en: Middle English plesen kept the verb and began to use it inside fixed courteous formulas.
items.cn: 中古英语的 plesen 保留了动词用法，并开始在固定的客套句式里使用它。

items.en: Modern English keeps please as a verb, splits off pleased and pleasant as adjectives, and uses the bare form as a courtesy marker.
items.cn: 现代英语让 please 继续作动词，分出 pleased 与 pleasant 两个形容词，又用光杆形式充当礼貌标记。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin verb for being agreeable; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for satisfying someone.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「令人合意」这一动词上的同族词；近义组收表示「使满意」的动词。

entries.definition: Feeling happy or satisfied about something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事感到高兴或满意的。

entries.definition: Enjoyable, agreeable or nice to be with.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；宜人的；好相处的。

entries.definition: To annoy or upset someone.

entries.definition: An urgent request, or the answer of an accused person in court.
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；被告在法庭上的答辩。

entries.definition: To give someone enough of what they want or need.

entries.definition: To give someone great pleasure.

entries.definition: To please someone greatly, often by being attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引并取悦某人。

entries.definition: To please someone by satisfying a wish or desire.
entries.definitionCN: 满足愿望而使某人高兴。

normalIntro.en: The family is built on one Latin verb for being agreeable, and its forms keep splitting into the feeling and the cause of the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词建立在同一个表示「令人合意」的拉丁动词上，各个形式不断分成「感受」和「引起感受之物」两侧。

normal.en: Latin placere means to be agreeable to someone, so what pleases is what the other person accepts as good.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 placere 意为「令某人觉得合意」，所以能 please 人的东西，就是被对方认可为好而接受的东西。

normal.en: Please yourself puts the same agreement inside the speaker: the wish you agree with is your own.
normal.cn: please yourself 把这种「合意」转向说话人自己：你认同的愿望就是你自己的愿望。

normal.en: Pleased with -ed describes how a person feels; pleasing with -ing describes what produces that feeling.
normal.cn: 加了 -ed 的 pleased 说人心里怎么感觉；加了 -ing 的 pleasing 说是什么东西造成了这种感觉。

normal.en: Pleasant came through French, so it lost the s of please but kept the sense of being agreeable.
normal.cn: pleasant 经由法语而来，因此丢了 please 里的 s，却保留了「合意、讨人喜欢」的意思。

normal.en: The bare please in a request is the old verb worn down to a single polite signal.
normal.cn: 请求句里那个单独的 please，是老动词被磨成了一个纯粹的礼貌信号。

abstract.en: A word that means both make happy and if you would shows that politeness is a small gift of comfort.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能表示「使高兴」又能表示「请」，说明礼貌本身就是送给对方的一点舒适。

abstract.en: Every please hands the decision to the listener for a second, and that second is what makes the request gentle.
abstract.cn: 每一次说 please，都是把决定权交给听者一小会儿，而这一小会儿正是请求变得柔和的原因。

abstract.en: A pleased face, a pleasant evening and a polite request all sit under one root, because all three are about things being acceptable.
abstract.cn: 满意的脸色、宜人的夜晚、客气的请求同出一根，因为三者说的都是「合意」。

examples.en: Please leave your shoes at the door.
examples.cn: 请把鞋留在门口。

examples.en: The children were pleased with the new playground.
examples.cn: 孩子们对新游乐场很满意。

examples.en: She learned to please herself instead of chasing approval.
examples.cn: 她学会按自己的心意生活，而不是一味追求别人的认可。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑利兹」——把好处扑过去让对方得利，就是「使高兴」；开口求人先递一个「请」。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使愉快、被接受）经古法语 plaisir 进入英语；同族词多与「合意、愉快」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is being agreeable to someone; from it grow the courteous request, the act of giving satisfaction, and the choice to follow one's own wish.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「令某人觉得合意」；由此长出礼貌请求、使人满意这两种用法，以及按自己心意行事的选择。

intro.cn: 一个表示「令人愉快」的拉丁动词撑起这一族词，两个英语后缀再把它分成「感受」与「成因」两侧。

definition_zh: 誓言；承诺；抵押物；发誓；抵押
definition_en: a serious promise, or something handed over as security for a debt, and the act of promising or depositing it
core_image: 举起的右手和一张写好的承诺书，说出口就要兑现
scene: 毕业典礼上，全体新生举起右手，跟着领誓人一句一句念出承诺。Each new member had to pledge loyalty to the group in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里用的是动词「郑重许诺」（第 3 个义项：发誓、保证）；句意为每位新成员都得当众承诺忠于这个团体。画面里有举起的右手、台下的同伴和安静下来的会场。

collocations.zh: 发誓献身于；保证致力于

derivatives.zh: 由 pledge 加表示承受方的后缀 -ee 构成，法律上指「接受质押的人」
由 pledge 加表示行为方的后缀 -or 构成，法律上指「出质人；抵押人」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pledge 的过去分词构成，义为「未作承诺的；未抵押的」

senses.title: A solemn promise
senses.definition: a serious promise that you will do something, especially one made in public
senses.definitionCN: 郑重许下、通常当众作出的承诺
senses.example: The government broke its pledge to protect the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 政府违背了保护这片森林的承诺。
senses.why: The word first named a thing handed over as a guarantee; a spoken promise borrowed that image because a word can also be held against you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指交出去的担保物；口头承诺借用同一意象，因为一句话同样可以日后被人拿来对着你算账。

senses.title: Something given as security
senses.definition: an object or sum left with someone as security until a debt is paid or a duty is met
senses.definitionCN: 为担保债务或义务而交给对方保管的物件或款项
senses.example: He left his watch as a pledge for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他把手表留下作为这笔借款的抵押。
senses.why: In medieval law a pledge was the item physically held, so the object and the promise shared one name from the start.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪的法律里，pledge 就是被实际扣在手里的那件东西，所以「物」与「诺」从一开始就共用一个名字。

senses.title: To promise solemnly
senses.definition: to promise seriously and publicly that you will do something or stay loyal
senses.definitionCN: 郑重而公开地保证要做某事或保持忠诚
senses.example: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司承诺把排放量削减一半。
senses.why: The verb grew out of the noun: to pledge is to hand over your word the way you hand over a security.
senses.whyCN: 动词是从名词长出来的：to pledge 就是把你的话交出去，方式正如交出一件担保物。

senses.title: To give something as security
senses.definition: to hand over an object or property as a guarantee for a loan
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或财产交出，作为借款的担保
senses.example: She pledged her house to raise money for the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 她抵押了房子，为诊所筹钱。
senses.why: Since the noun named the security itself, the verb could name the act of depositing it, which is why finance keeps this concrete sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指的就是担保物本身，动词自然可以指「把它交出去」这个动作，所以金融语境里这个具体义项一直活着。

intro.en: Pledge entered English through French as a legal word for a surety, and it is generally thought to go back to a Germanic root rather than to Latin.
intro.cn: pledge 作为法律用语经法语进入英语，本义是「担保」；一般认为它源自日耳曼词根，而非拉丁语。

items.en: Old French plege meant a surety, both the promise and the person or object standing behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 plege 意为担保，既指承诺，也指为承诺作保的人或物。

items.en: The word is generally thought to come from a reconstructed Frankish form plegan, meaning to stand surety; the asterisk marks a form not directly recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词来自法兰克语的重构形式 plegan，义为「担保、负责」；带星号表示这是重构而非直接见于文献的形式。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word into law and trade, where a pledge could be a hostage, a deposit or a formal promise.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词用于法律与交易，pledge 可以是人质、押金，也可以是正式承诺。

items.en: The sense widened from property to conduct, so people began to pledge loyalty, support and good behaviour.
items.cn: 词义从财物扩展到行为，于是人们开始 pledge 忠诚、支持与良好表现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the legal deposit sense and the public promise sense side by side, from pawnshops to election campaigns.
items.cn: 现代英语让「抵押」与「公开承诺」两个义项并存，从当铺一直用到竞选。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers guarantee words built on the same French or Germanic stock; the near-meaning group gathers words for promises and security.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一法语或日耳曼语来源上的担保类词；近义组收表示承诺与担保的词。

entries.definition: The Old French form from which the English word descends.
entries.definitionCN: 英语词所由来的古法语形式。

entries.definition: To beg or argue a case in court; it looks close but comes from a different Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；在法庭上申辩。只是拼写相近，词源来自另一个拉丁名词。

entries.definition: The person who receives a pledge as security.
entries.definitionCN: 接受质押物的一方。

entries.definition: The person who gives property as security.
entries.definitionCN: 交出财产作担保的一方。

entries.definition: A statement that you will certainly do something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示一定会做某事的说法。

entries.definition: A very solemn promise, often religious.
entries.definitionCN: 极郑重的誓言，常带宗教色彩。

entries.definition: A firm assurance that something will happen or work.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事会发生或有效的明确保证。

entries.definition: Money or an item left as security.
entries.definitionCN: 作为担保留下的钱或物。

entries.definition: Property promised to a lender if a loan is not repaid.
entries.definitionCN: 借款不能偿还时交给贷方的抵押财产。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the object held against a debt and grew into the spoken promise that carries the same weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初指被扣下抵债的物件，后来长成同样有分量的口头承诺。

normal.en: A pledge was first a thing left with someone, so the physical image of handing something over is still inside the word.
normal.cn: pledge 最早是留在别人手里的东西，所以「把东西交出去」这个具体画面至今仍藏在词里。

normal.en: Make a pledge uses the noun pattern, while pledge to do uses the verb pattern, and both keep the idea of a binding word.
normal.cn: make a pledge 走名词结构，pledge to do 走动词结构，两者都保留了「话一出口就有约束力」的意思。

normal.en: Election pledge shows the word in public politics, where a promise is made to be judged by voters.
normal.cn: election pledge 把这个词放进公共政治，那里的承诺说出口就是为了让选民日后检验。

normal.en: Pledge oneself to adds a reflexive object, stressing that the speaker personally takes on the duty.
normal.cn: pledge oneself to 加了反身宾语，强调说话人本人把这副担子接了下来。

normal.en: The legal pair pledgee and pledgor splits the two sides of the same security arrangement.
normal.cn: 法律上成对的 pledgee 与 pledgor 把同一项担保安排的两端分开了。

abstract.en: A word for a held object turning into a word for a spoken promise shows how much of trust is about having something at stake.
abstract.cn: 一个指「被扣下的物件」的词转成指「说出的话」，说明信任很大程度上取决于有没有东西押在那里。

abstract.en: Every pledge creates a future that other people are allowed to expect.
abstract.cn: 每一次承诺都造出一个别人有权期待的将来。

abstract.en: The same word covers a pawned watch and a campaign promise because both are securities offered against doubt.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指当掉的手表也指竞选承诺，因为两者都是用来对付怀疑的担保。

examples.en: The government broke its pledge to protect the forest.
examples.cn: 政府违背了保护这片森林的承诺。

examples.en: He left his watch as a pledge for the loan.
examples.cn: 他把手表留下作为这笔借款的抵押。

examples.en: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.
examples.cn: 这家公司承诺把排放量削减一半。

root: 古法语 plege（担保）进入英语；一般认为可上溯到法兰克语重构形式 plegan（担保、负责），属日耳曼来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a guarantee held by someone else; it splits into the object deposited and the solemn word given, each with its own noun and verb use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「交到别人手里的担保」；它分成押出去的实物与说出口的郑重的话，两者又各有名词与动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised right hand beside a written promise that must be kept.
core.cn: 核心意象：举起的右手旁边放着一份必须兑现的承诺书。

intro.en: There is no secure Latin family behind this word; its parts come from French and Germanic sources, with English suffixes building the legal pair.
intro.cn: 这个词背后没有可靠的拉丁词族；它的构件来自法语与日耳曼语，再由英语后缀造出法律上一对身份词。

latinIntro.en: A Latin form is sometimes proposed as an intermediate, but it is itself borrowed from Germanic, so no genuine Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 也有人提出过某个拉丁语中间形式，但它本身借自日耳曼语，因此这里不列真正的拉丁同族词。

scene: 秋收过后的谷仓里，麻袋一直码到房梁，农户随手还能再拖下一袋。A plentiful harvest meant the village would not worry about food that winter.
sceneCN: 这里说的是「丰产的、物产多的」（第 2 个义项）；句意为丰收让全村那个冬天都不用为吃食发愁。画面里有谷仓、码高的麻袋和堆到门口的谷物。

pos.zh: 充足的；丰富的；丰产的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 由 plentiful 加 -ly 构成，义为「充足地；大量地」
由 plentiful 加 -ness 构成，义为「充足；丰富」
由 plenty 的词干加 -eous 构成，文学用语，义为「丰盛的」
借拉丁 plenitudo 而来，与 plentiful 同源，义为「丰足；充满」

senses.title: More than enough for the need
senses.definition: present in an amount large enough to cover what is needed, usually with something to spare
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到足以满足需要，通常还有富余
senses.example: The clinic has a plentiful supply of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所的干净用水供应充足。
senses.why: The adjective is plenty plus -ful, so it describes a supply that is literally full rather than merely adequate.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由名词 plenty 加 -ful 构成，字面就是「满满的」，强调的不是刚好够用，而是有余。

senses.title: Yielding a large amount
senses.definition: producing a large amount of something, said of land, a season, a harvest or a region
senses.definitionCN: 产出很多东西，用来形容土地、季节、收成或地区
senses.example: The valley is famous for its plentiful fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 这道山谷以盛产水果闻名。
senses.why: Land and seasons are judged by what they give, so the same word moves from the size of a supply to the generosity of its source.
senses.whyCN: 土地和季节是按它们给出的东西来评价的，于是这个词从「供给多」滑到「源头慷慨」。

senses.title: Present in large numbers
senses.titleCN: 大量存在的；为数众多的
senses.definition: found in large numbers, as with examples, opportunities or mistakes rather than physical goods
senses.definitionCN: 数量很多地存在，多用于例子、机会、错误等，而非具体货物
senses.example: Plentiful examples make the grammar rule easier to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 大量例子让这条语法规则更容易记住。
senses.why: Once the word means an oversized amount, it can count anything that keeps appearing, not only goods stacked on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦表示「数量超出所需」，凡是一再出现的东西都能用它来数，不再限于货架上的货品。

intro.en: Plentiful is the adjective built on the noun plenty, and both go back through French to a Latin adjective meaning full.
intro.cn: plentiful 是在名词 plenty 上加后缀构成的形容词，二者都经法语上溯到一个意为「满的」的拉丁形容词。

items.en: Plenus meant full, and it is the root behind both plenty and plentiful.
items.cn: plenus 意为「满的」，是 plenty 与 plentiful 共同的根。

items.en: The noun plenitas named fullness or abundance, the state of being full.
items.cn: 名词 plenitas 指「满、充足」，也就是处于装满的状态。

items.en: Old French plente carried that abundance into French and was used of crops, food and wealth.
items.cn: 古法语 plente 把这层「充足」带入法语，常用于庄稼、食物与财富。

items.en: Middle English took plente as a noun for abundance and later formed an adjective from it.
items.cn: 中古英语把 plente 借作表示「充足」的名词，后来又由它造出形容词。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling plentiful, using -ful to say that something is full of plenty.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 plentiful，用 -ful 表示「充满 plenty」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the nouns and adjectives of the Latin full family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for large amounts.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「满」这一族的名称与形容词；近义组收表示「数量多」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective, meaning a large amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的名词，义为「大量；充足」。

entries.definition: An older adjective for abundant, now mostly literary.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的「丰盛」形容词，现多为文学用语。

entries.definition: The state of being full or complete.
entries.definitionCN: 满盈、充足的状态。

entries.definition: Full or complete, as in a meeting with all members present.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的；全体出席的。

entries.definition: Existing in large quantities, often more formally than plentiful.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在的，比 plentiful 更正式。

entries.definition: Enough and often more than enough for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 足够且常有富余的。

entries.definition: Produced in large amounts, especially of writing or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 大量产生的，多指文字或笔记。

entries.definition: Generous and giving a lot, often of a harvest.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨而丰盛的，多形容收成。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is simply the noun plenty wearing the suffix -ful, so every image of a full storehouse belongs to it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词就是名词 plenty 披上 -ful 这件外套，所以凡是「满仓」的画面都归它管。

normal.en: Plentiful is plenty plus -ful, so the ending says full of plenty rather than merely enough.
normal.cn: plentiful 就是 plenty 加 -ful，后缀表明的是「充满大量」，而不只是「够用」。

normal.en: The Latin root plenus, meaning full, also hides inside plenary and plenitude, which both stress completeness.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 plenus 意为「满」，也藏在 plenary 与 plenitude 里，两者都强调「完备」。

normal.en: Plentiful goes with supplies and harvests, because it measures a stock rather than a single object.
normal.cn: plentiful 常与 supply、harvest 一类词搭配，因为它衡量的是存量，而不是单个物件。

normal.en: The adverb plentifully keeps the same meaning and simply adds the manner of giving.
normal.cn: 副词 plentifully 意思不变，只是补上「以何种方式给予」。

normal.en: Unlike plenty, the adjective cannot stand alone before a noun without naming what is abundant.
normal.cn: 与名词 plenty 不同，这个形容词放在名词前时，必须说清是什么东西充足。

abstract.en: A word built from full describes not just quantity but the relief of not having to count.
abstract.cn: 一个由「满」构成的词，描述的不只是数量，还有不必再数的安心。

abstract.en: Plentiful land is judged by what it gives away, which is why the same word can praise a valley.
abstract.cn: 丰饶的土地是按它给出的东西来评价的，所以同一个词也能用来夸一道山谷。

abstract.en: When examples are plentiful, abundance stops being about food and becomes about chances to learn.
abstract.cn: 当例子变得 plentiful，充足就不再关乎食物，而关乎学习的机会。

examples.en: The clinic has a plentiful supply of clean water.
examples.cn: 诊所的干净用水供应充足。

examples.en: The valley is famous for its plentiful fruit.
examples.cn: 这道山谷以盛产水果闻名。

examples.en: Plentiful examples make the grammar rule easier to remember.
examples.cn: 大量例子让这条语法规则更容易记住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱提否」——粮袋扑棱棱堆到提不动，多到让人直说「否」也不必愁，就是 plentiful。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ plenitas（充足）→ 古法语 plente → 英语名词 plenty，再加后缀 -ful 构成 plentiful。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a stock that is more than full; from it come the producing land, and then any set of repeated instances.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装得满满的存量」；由此分出丰产的土地，再扩展到任何一再出现的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks stacked to the roof of a barn, with another one still within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：麻袋一直码到谷仓屋顶，伸手还够得着下一袋。

branches.en: a water tank filled past the mark
branches.cn: 水罐装到刻度线以上

branches.en: orchard trees bending under fruit
branches.cn: 果树被果实压弯

branches.en: margins crowded with worked examples
branches.cn: 页边写满例题

branches.en: a market table that is never empty
branches.cn: 始终不空的集市摊子

branches.en: a season of good weather and good yields
branches.cn: 风调雨顺又高产的一季

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin adjective of fullness plus an English suffix of fullness, which is why the word doubles the idea of being full.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁语的「满」加上英语表示「充满」的后缀构成，所以它把「满」这层意思叠了两遍。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 情节；小块土地；密谋；绘制；标出
definition_en: the arranged sequence of events in a story; a small measured piece of land; a secret plan made by a group; and to mark a course or a set of data on a map or graph
core_image: 田埂围出一小块地，旁边有人低头在纸上描出一条曲线
scene: 剧本读到一半，作者在页边画出一个方框，把人物下一步的动作圈了进去。She sketched the plot of her next novel on the back of an envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 plot 是「情节」（第 1 个义项：故事中事件的安排）；句意为她在信封背面勾勒出下一部小说的情节。图中可辨识物件：剧本、页边方框、信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 plot 双写末尾的 t 加表示「人或工具」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「密谋者；绘图仪」
由 plot 加 -ing 构成，义为「密谋；绘图」
由前缀 sub-（在下、次要）加 plot 构成，义为「次要情节」

senses.title: The sequence of events in a story
senses.definition: the organized sequence of events and actions that makes up a story, play or film
senses.definitionCN: 构成小说、戏剧或电影的故事事件与行动的有序安排
senses.example: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。
senses.why: Plot first named a piece of ground marked off by boundaries, and a story line is likewise a stretch staked out by the writer: a beginning, a turn and an end. The sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when critics needed a word for the arrangement of incidents in a play.
senses.whyCN: plot 最初指用界线围出的一块地，而故事线同样是一段由作者圈定的范围：开端、转折与结局。这个义项在十七世纪有记录，当时评论家需要一个词来指戏剧中事件的安排。

senses.title: A small measured piece of land
senses.definition: a small area of ground marked out for a particular use, such as building a house or growing vegetables
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途（如盖房或种菜）而划出的一小块土地
senses.example: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后一小块窄地上种豆子。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, most likely because the patch had been marked off from the rest. The measuring of land by lines is still visible in a garden plot or a building plot.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最古老义项：古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，很可能因为这片地被从周围划了出来。用线划分土地的动作至今仍看得见，比如菜地或建筑用地。

senses.title: A secret plan made by several people
senses.definition: a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or unlawful
senses.definitionCN: 一群人暗中策划做有害或违法之事的计划
senses.example: The police uncovered a plot to rob the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 警方破获了一起抢劫银行的阴谋。
senses.why: English speakers blended the native land word with Old French complot, a group scheme; the two forms merged in sound and meaning, so the idea of a secret scheme attached itself to plot and has stayed ever since.
senses.whyCN: 说英语的人把本土表示土地的那个词与古法语 complot（一伙人的图谋）混同，两个形式在读音和意义上合流，于是「暗中图谋」的意思就附着在 plot 上，一直留到今天。

senses.title: To mark a course or data on a graph
senses.definition: to mark points, a line or a course on a map or graph, or to follow and record a moving path
senses.definitionCN: 在地图或图表上标出点、线或路线，或跟踪记录一条移动的轨迹
senses.example: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。
senses.why: Marking points on a sheet repeats on paper the old act of marking ground. Sailors plotted a course by laying it out point by point, and the same verb now covers data points drawn on a graph.
senses.whyCN: 在纸上标出各个点，等于把当年在土地上做记号的动作重做一遍。水手靠逐点标出来绘制航线，同一个动词如今也用于把数据点画成图表。

intro.en: Plot is an old English word for a piece of ground whose earlier origin is uncertain; the sense of a secret scheme came from French complot, and the story sense grew out of the marked-out ground.
intro.cn: plot 是英语中表示一块土地的古老词，更早的来源不确定；「阴谋」的意思来自法语 complot，而「情节」的意思则从划出来的那块地引申而来。

items.en: Old English plot named a definite piece of ground, and its earlier origin is uncertain; it may have meant a patch marked off from the rest.
items.cn: 古英语 plot 指一块界限明确的地，更早的来源不确定，可能指从周围划出来的一小片。

items.en: Middle English used plot for a small field or a measured patch, and the word stayed close to land and boundaries.
items.cn: 中古英语用 plot 指小田地或量好的一小块地，词义始终离不开土地与界线。

items.en: Old French complot meant a group scheme or conspiracy; English speakers heard it as the same word as plot and merged the two meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 complot 指一伙人的图谋或阴谋；说英语的人把它听成与 plot 同一个词，两种意思便合在一起。

items.en: In the sixteenth century plot could mean a secret plan, and by the seventeenth critics used it for the arranged incidents of a play.
items.cn: 十六世纪时 plot 已可指秘密计划，到十七世纪评论家又用它指戏剧中安排好的事件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the land, the scheme and the story, and adds the verb of charting a course or plotting data.
items.cn: 现代英语保留土地、阴谋与故事三层意思，又加上绘制航线或标绘数据的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers this word's own family plus the French cousin behind the conspiratorial sense; the near-meaning group gathers words for a story line, a scheme and a patch of ground.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及带来「阴谋」义的那个法语近亲；近义组收表示故事线、图谋与小块地的词。

entries.definition: An old word for a group conspiracy, borrowed from French and now almost out of use.
entries.definitionCN: 指一伙人阴谋的旧词，借自法语，如今几乎不再使用。

entries.definition: A person who makes a secret plan, or a machine that draws graphs.
entries.definitionCN: 密谋的人，或绘制图表的机器；绘图仪。

entries.definition: A secondary story line running beside the main one.
entries.definitionCN: 与主线并行的一条次要情节。

entries.definition: The main sequence of events in a story, seen as a line.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中主要事件的走向，被看作一条线。

entries.definition: The main line of events in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中事件的主线。

entries.definition: A plan, often a secret or a clever one.
entries.definitionCN: 计划，常指秘密或巧妙的安排。

entries.definition: A small piece of ground, especially one used for growing something.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块土地，尤指用来种东西的。

entries.definition: A secret plan by several people to do something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 数人暗中策划做坏事的图谋。

normalIntro.en: The word began as ground marked off by lines, and that single picture of a bounded patch keeps reappearing: a patch of soil, a stretch of events, a set of points on a sheet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从被线条划出的土地开始，而「一块有边界的范围」这个画面反复出现：一块土、一段事件、纸上一组点。

normal.en: Old English plot meant a measured piece of ground, so the garden plot and the building plot are the oldest uses of the word.
normal.cn: 古英语 plot 指量好的一块地，所以菜地与建筑用地是这个词最古老的用法。

normal.en: A story plot is a stretch of events with a boundary: the writer decides where the tale starts and where it stops.
normal.cn: 故事的情节是一段有边界的事件：作者决定故事从哪里开始、到哪里结束。

normal.en: The conspiratorial sense came from French complot, which English speakers heard as the same word and merged with plot.
normal.cn: 阴谋义来自法语 complot，说英语的人把它听成同一个词，于是与 plot 合并。

normal.en: To plot a graph is to mark points one by one, the way a surveyor marks a patch of ground.
normal.cn: plot 一张图就是逐个标出点，正如测量员标出一块地。

normal.en: Subplot adds sub-, meaning under or secondary, so it names a story line running beneath the main one.
normal.cn: subplot 加了表示「在下、次要」的 sub-，指主线之下的一条情节。

abstract.en: A plot is a line drawn around a piece of the world so that attention can settle there.
abstract.cn: 情节是围绕世界的一小块画出的线，好让注意力落在那里。

abstract.en: The same word holds a garden and a conspiracy, because both are marked out in advance by someone who intends to use them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着菜地也装着阴谋，因为两者都是有人事先划出来、打算加以利用的。

abstract.en: On a graph, a plot is a promise that a movement can be turned into a shape.
abstract.cn: 在图表上，一条绘出的曲线是一个承诺：一段运动可以被变成形状。

examples.en: The plot turns on a letter that never arrives.
examples.cn: 情节的关键是一封始终没有送达的信。

examples.en: They grow beans on a narrow plot behind the house.

examples.en: The software plots the temperature against the hour.
examples.cn: 这个软件把温度随时间的变化绘成曲线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑络」——线索一条条扑上来，又络在一起，故事就有了情节；记住 plot 是情节，也是小块地。

root: 古英语 plot 指一块划定的土地，更早来源不确定；表示「阴谋」的意思受古法语 complot 影响而合流；表示「情节」的意思在十七世纪从「划出的一段范围」引申出来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bounded patch; the senses run from a measured piece of land, to a stretch of events marked out by a writer, to a scheme hatched in secret, and finally to points marked on a sheet.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一块有边界的范围；义项从量好的土地，走到作者划出的一段事件，再到暗中策划的图谋，最后落到纸上标出的点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small field fenced by ridges, and a hand tracing a curve beside it on paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：田埂围出的一小块地，旁边有人在纸上描出一条曲线。

branches.cn: 一串事件因一封信而转向

intro.en: The word is a native English noun of uncertain origin whose family grew by prefixes and suffixes, while the conspiratorial sense leans on a French cousin.

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the land sense, whose origin is uncertain; the conspiracy sense came through French from a form whose own source is also disputed.

definition_zh: 加；加上；再加；正的；有利的；优势
definition_en: used between two amounts to show addition; added on top of what is already there; greater than zero or favourable; and an advantage that counts in someone's favour

scene: 账单摊在桌子中央，服务员把最后一道菜名也添在末尾。The bill came to forty pounds, plus a small service charge.

senses.title: Added to an amount
senses.definition: used between two numbers or amounts to show that the second is added to the first
