senses.example: Two plus three makes five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: Latin plus meant more, and arithmetic borrowed the word to stand at the exact point where one quantity becomes more by taking in another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 plus 意为「更多」，算术把这个词放在一个数量因并入另一个而变多的那个位置上。

senses.title: In addition to what is mentioned
senses.definition: used after a statement to add something further that is also included
senses.definitionCN: 在一句话之后补充还有某项东西也算在内
senses.example: The room has a balcony, plus a view of the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间带阳台，另外还能看到港口。
senses.why: If plus can add one number to another, it can also add one fact to another, so the word moves from counting to piling extra items onto a statement.
senses.whyCN: 既然 plus 能把一个数加到另一个数上，也就能把一件事加进另一句话，于是这个词从算数走到了在陈述上追加条件。

senses.title: Above zero or favourable
senses.definition: greater than zero, or working in one's favour rather than against it
senses.definitionCN: 大于零的，或对人有利而不是不利的
senses.example: A plus factor is that the school is within walking distance.
senses.exampleCN: 一个有利因素是学校走几步就到。
senses.why: On a scale with zero in the middle, whatever falls on the higher side is marked with a plus, and from that mark the word comes to mean anything that counts for you.
senses.whyCN: 在以零为中点的刻度上，落在较高一侧的都标上加号，从这个记号起，这个词就用来指任何对你有利的东西。

senses.title: An advantage
senses.definition: a quality or circumstance that gives someone an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 能让人占上风的某种长处或条件
senses.example: Speaking two languages is a real plus in this job.
senses.exampleCN: 会两种语言在这份工作里是真正的优势。
senses.why: Once a plus marks what lies on the good side of zero, the mark itself becomes a noun for the good thing it stands for, which is why a strength is simply called a plus.
senses.whyCN: 当加号用来标出零以上的那一侧，这个记号本身就变成了名词，指它所代表的好处，所以一项长处直接被叫作 a plus。

intro.en: Plus is a Latin comparative meaning more, and English took it over unchanged for arithmetic before widening it to extra items, positive values and personal advantages.
intro.cn: plus 是拉丁语中表示「更多」的比较级形式，英语原样借来用于算术，随后扩展到额外的项目、正值与个人优势。

items.en: Plus meant more, and Roman writers used it in phrases of addition and comparison long before any symbol existed.
items.cn: plus 意为更多，早在任何符号出现之前，罗马作家就用它来表示添加与比较。

items.en: The stem behind plus is plures, more or several, which also gave the adjective pluralis and English plural.
items.cn: plus 背后的词干是 plures，意为更多、数个，它同时给出了形容词 pluralis 与英语的 plural。

items.en: English borrowed plus in arithmetic and surveying, where it named the operation of adding rather than a written sign.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪把 plus 借入算术与测量，当时它指添加这个运算，而不是一个写出来的符号。

items.en: The cross-shaped mark for addition was read aloud as plus, so the sign and the word became inseparable in schoolroom practice.
items.cn: 表示相加的十字形记号被读作 plus，符号与词在课堂练习里从此分不开。

items.en: Modern English uses plus for extra items, for positive numbers and results, and, as a noun, for any advantage a person or plan holds.
items.cn: 现代英语用 plus 表示额外项目、正值与好结果，并作名词指人或方案拥有的任何优势。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem for more and adds two words that merely share letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for addition and for an extra benefit.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语表示「更多」的词干展开，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收表示添加与额外好处的词。

entries.definition: An amount left over after what is needed has been used; it joins sur-, over, to the Latin stem of plus.
entries.definitionCN: 需要之外剩下的数量；由表示「超过」的 sur- 加 plus 的拉丁词干构成。

entries.definition: The form of a word used for more than one thing; it comes from the same Latin stem plures.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表示多于一个事物的词形；来自同一个拉丁词干 plures。

entries.definition: A thick soft fabric, or a word for something luxurious; it looks like plus but comes from a different French source.
entries.definitionCN: 厚而柔软的织物，也形容奢华；拼写与 plus 相近，却来自另一个法语来源，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft round fruit with a stone; the resemblance is spelling only, since the fruit name has another origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一种带核的柔软圆果；只是拼写相像，这个水果名另有来源。

entries.definition: The act of adding something, or the thing that is added.
entries.definitionCN: 添加的行为，或被添加上去的东西。

entries.definition: An extra amount given beyond what is usual or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 在通常或预期之外额外给出的东西。

entries.definition: Something that puts a person in a better position than others.
entries.definitionCN: 使人比他人处于更有利地位的东西。

entries.definition: More than the usual or expected amount, or something added.
entries.definitionCN: 多于通常或预期的，或额外添加的东西。

normalIntro.en: One Latin comparative, more, supplies the whole family: the arithmetic word, the leftover noun, the plural form and the noun for an advantage.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语比较级「更多」撑起整族词：算术里的加、剩下的名词、复数形式，以及表示优势的名词。

normal.en: Latin plus means more, so the word sits exactly where a quantity grows by taking in another.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plus 意为更多，所以这个词正待在一个数量因并入另一个而变多的位置上。

normal.en: Surplus is sur-, over, plus the same stem: the amount that goes beyond what was needed.
normal.cn: surplus 是表示「超过」的 sur- 加上同一词干，指超出所需的那部分。

normal.en: Plural comes from plures, more than one, which is the same comparative family as plus.
normal.cn: plural 来自 plures（多于一个），与 plus 属于同一个比较级词族。

normal.en: On the plus side is arithmetic turned into judgement: the entries that count in your favour.
normal.cn: on the plus side 是把算术变成判断：那些算在你名下的有利条目。

normal.en: Plus never changes shape: no plural pluses in the arithmetic sense, no past tense, no comparative.
normal.cn: plus 从不改变形态：算术义没有复数，没有过去式，也没有比较级。

abstract.en: A plus is a small hook that pulls the next thing in, which is why it can join numbers and facts alike.
abstract.cn: 加号像一个小钩子，把下一件东西拉进来，所以它能连接数字，也能连接事实。

abstract.en: An advantage is arithmetic done on a life: what is added to your side of the ledger.
abstract.cn: 优势是对人生做的一次算术：添到你这一栏里的东西。

abstract.en: Zero is only a line, and everything on one side of it wears the same mark.
abstract.cn: 零只是一条线，落在它同一侧的东西都带着同一个记号。

examples.en: Two plus three makes five.
examples.cn: 二加三等于五。

examples.en: The rent is three hundred a month, plus electricity.
examples.cn: 房租每月三百，外加电费。

examples.en: A real plus of the flat is the morning light.
examples.cn: 这套房子真正的优点是有早晨的阳光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉丝」——把一根丝线普普通通地拉过来接上，就多出一段；记住 plus 是加。

root: 拉丁语 plus（更多）为比较级形式，词干 plures 意为更多、数个，同族有 surplus（超过之后的剩余）、plural（复数）。英语于十六七世纪借入 plus 用于算术，后引申为正值、额外项目与优势。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one quantity taking in another and becoming more; the senses run from arithmetic addition, to an extra item in a statement, to the positive side of a scale, and finally to a personal advantage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个数量并入另一个而变多；义项从算术上的相加，走到陈述里追加的一项，再到刻度上为正的一侧，最后落到个人的优势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pebble on a counting board pushed against another so the two piles become one larger pile.
core.cn: 核心意象：算板上一颗石子被推向另一颗，两堆并成一堆更大的。

branches.en: two pebbles pushed together on a counting board
branches.cn: 算板上并到一起的两颗石子

branches.en: one more name written at the end of a list
branches.cn: 名单末尾又添上的一个名字

branches.en: a thermometer standing above the zero mark
branches.cn: 温度计停在零度线以上

branches.en: a favourable entry in the account book
branches.cn: 账本上一笔有利的记录

branches.en: a second language counted as a strength
branches.cn: 被算作长处的一门第二语言

intro.en: The word is a Latin comparative of quantity, and the family grows by putting prefixes and suffixes around that one stem for more.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示数量的比较级，整族词都是在那一个表示「更多」的词干前后加前缀后缀长出来的。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for this word: the comparative plus, more, and its stem plures, more or several.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词有可考的拉丁形式：比较级 plus（更多）及其词干 plures（更多、数个）。

items.meaning: the state of being many, or a majority

definition_zh: 肺炎；肺部炎症；急性肺部感染
definition_en: an infection or inflammation of the lungs that fills the air sacs with fluid and makes breathing hard
core_image: 肺泡里积了水，每次呼吸都像隔着湿棉花吹气
scene: 冬夜里，老人咳出一口带血的痰，额头烧得发烫。The doctor heard crackles in his chest and sent him to hospital with pneumonia.
sceneCN: 这里 pneumonia 是「急性肺部感染」（第 2 个义项：发烧、咳嗽、需要就医的那一种肺炎）；句意为医生听出他胸中的湿啰音，以肺炎把他送进了医院。

collocations.zh: 轻型肺炎（仍能下地行走的非典型肺炎）

derivatives.zh: 肺的；肺炎的；由 pneumon（肺）加 -ic 构成
肺组织的炎症；pneumon 加 -itis（炎症），所指比肺炎更窄
支气管肺炎；由 bronch-（气管）与 pneumonia 复合而成

senses.title: Inflammation of the lungs
senses.definition: any inflammation of the lung tissue, whatever germ or irritant has caused it
senses.definitionCN: 不论由何种病菌或刺激物引起，肺组织出现的炎症
senses.example: Pneumonia can follow a viral infection or appear on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 肺炎可能继发于病毒感染，也可能单独出现。
senses.why: Greek pneumon named the lung as the breathing organ, and the ending -ia named a condition of it, so the word first described a diseased lung rather than a germ.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 pneumon 把肺命名为「呼吸的器官」，词尾 -ia 表示某种状态，所以这个词最初描述的是「有病的肺」，而不是某种病菌。

senses.title: The acute infectious illness
senses.definition: a sudden infection of the lungs with fever, cough and chest pain, usually needing medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 以发热、咳嗽和胸痛为表现的急性肺部感染，通常需要就医治疗
senses.example: He was admitted with pneumonia after two days of high fever.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧两天之后，他因肺炎住进了医院。
senses.why: Once doctors learned that germs cause it, the same word came to name the illness a patient actually feels, with its fever and its cough.
senses.whyCN: 当医生弄清了病菌才是病因，同一个词就开始命名患者真正感受到的那场病，连同它的发热与咳嗽。

senses.title: A single infected lobe
senses.definition: one localized area of infected lung tissue, as seen on a chest image or heard through a stethoscope
senses.definitionCN: 某一肺叶或某一片肺组织上的感染病灶，可在胸片或听诊中定位
senses.example: The scan showed pneumonia in the lower lobe of the right lung.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示右肺下叶有肺炎病灶。
senses.why: Because the infection often settles in one lobe, doctors use the same noun for the patch as for the whole disease.
senses.whyCN: 因为感染常常落在一个肺叶里，医生就用同一个名词既指那片病灶，也指整个疾病。

senses.title: Walking pneumonia
senses.definition: a mild form of pneumonia in which the patient stays active and the symptoms are easily mistaken for a cold
senses.definitionCN: 症状较轻、患者仍能活动、容易被当成感冒的一种肺炎
senses.example: Walking pneumonia rarely puts a healthy adult to bed.
senses.exampleCN: 轻型肺炎很少让健康的成年人卧床。
senses.why: The nickname was coined because these patients could still walk about, so the illness hid behind its mildness.
senses.whyCN: 这个绰号来自患者仍能四处走动，于是疾病就藏在轻微的症状后面。

senses.title: The friend of the aged
senses.titleCN: 终末期肺炎；旧称「老人的朋友」
senses.definition: pneumonia seen as the last illness of a frail elderly person, sometimes described as a short and merciful ending
senses.definitionCN: 体弱老人临终时所患的肺炎，旧时被说成一种短暂而少折磨的结局
senses.example: Old doctors sometimes called pneumonia the friend of the aged.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的医生有时把肺炎称作「老人的朋友」。
senses.why: In an age without antibiotics, pneumonia could close a long illness quickly, so the word carried a strange comfort as well as fear.
senses.whyCN: 在没有抗生素的年代，肺炎能很快结束一场漫长的病，于是这个词既带着恐惧，也带着一点奇怪的安慰。

intro.en: Pneumonia comes from Greek pneumon, the lung, a word itself built on pneuma, breath or air.
intro.cn: pneumonia 来自希腊语 pneumon（肺），而这个词本身又由 pneuma（气息、风）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root for breathing or blowing is generally thought to lie behind pneuma; the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 pneuma 背后有一个表示「呼吸、吹」的原始印欧语重构词根；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Pneuma meant breath, air or wind, and it also named the breath of life.
items.cn: pneuma 指气息、空气或风，也用来指生命的气息。

items.en: Pneumon named the lung, literally the organ of breathing.
items.cn: pneumon 指肺，字面意思就是「用来呼吸的器官」。

items.en: Hippocratic writers used pneumonia for a disease of the lungs, and the -ia ending marked a condition.
items.cn: 希波克拉底学派的作者用 pneumonia 指肺部疾病，-ia 词尾表示某种状态。

items.en: Medical Latin kept the Greek word almost unchanged, including the pn- cluster that English now pronounces without the p.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语几乎原样保留了希腊词，连英语如今不发音的 pn- 也留着。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin term in the seventeenth century, and it has named the disease ever since.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个拉丁词，此后一直用它命名这种病。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Greek lung root in view, while the near-meaning group sorts pneumonia from the lung diseases it is often confused with.
note.cn: 形近组围绕希腊语「肺」这个词根；近义组则把肺炎与常被混淆的肺部疾病分开。

entries.definition: relating to the lungs or to pneumonia
entries.definitionCN: 与肺或肺炎有关的；由 pneumonia 加 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: inflammation of the lung tissue itself
entries.definitionCN: 肺组织本身的炎症；与 pneumonia 同源，但 -itis 强调炎症而非感染。

entries.definition: worked by air or gas
entries.definitionCN: 靠空气或气体工作的；与肺炎同出 pneuma 一词，词义已转向「气」。

entries.definition: inflammation of the larger airways
entries.definitionCN: 较大气道的炎症，病变在气管分支而不在肺泡。

entries.definition: a bacterial infection that damages the lungs over a long period
entries.definitionCN: 长期损害肺部的细菌感染，病程比肺炎慢得多。

entries.definition: inflammation of the membrane around the lungs
entries.definitionCN: 肺外那层胸膜的炎症，痛在胸侧而不在肺泡里。

normalIntro.en: Pneumonia is a Greek lung word, so its parts point to breath and to the organ that does the breathing.
normalIntro.cn: pneumonia 是希腊语的「肺」词，它的各部分都指向呼吸和负责呼吸的那个器官。

normal.en: The pn- at the start is kept from Greek, so the p is silent and the word begins with a nyu sound.
normal.cn: 开头的 pn- 是从希腊语保留下来的，所以 p 不发音，词从「nyu」这个音开始。

normal.en: Pneumon means lung and -ia means a condition, so pneumonia is a condition of the lung.
normal.cn: pneumon 是肺，-ia 表示某种状态，所以 pneumonia 就是「肺的病态」。

normal.en: Pneumonic is the adjective, and pneumonitis is inflammation of the tissue rather than of the air sacs.
normal.cn: pneumonic 是形容词，pneumonitis 指肺组织的炎症，与肺泡里的肺炎不同。

normal.en: Walking pneumonia is mild enough that the patient keeps walking around.
normal.cn: walking pneumonia 症状轻，患者还能照常走动。

normal.en: Double pneumonia means both lungs are infected, not twice the severity of one lung.
normal.cn: double pneumonia 指两侧肺都受感染，不是单侧病情的两倍。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge soaked with water, and every squeeze makes a wet crackle.
abstract.cn: 想象一块吸满水的海绵，每捏一下都发出湿漉漉的响声。

abstract.en: Imagine a feverish patient propped on pillows, coughing until the chest hurts.
abstract.cn: 想象一位发烧的病人靠着枕头，咳到胸口发痛。

abstract.en: Think of a chest image with one white patch marking the infected lobe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张胸片上有一块白影，标出受感染的那个肺叶。

examples.en: Pneumonia is more dangerous in very young children and in the elderly.
examples.cn: 肺炎在幼儿和老人身上更危险。

examples.en: She recovered from pneumonia after a week of antibiotics.
examples.cn: 用了一周抗生素后，她的肺炎痊愈了。

examples.en: Doctors listen for crackles, one of the signs of pneumonia.
examples.cn: 医生听诊寻找湿啰音，那是肺炎的体征之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛摸你呀」——像有人摸一下胸口就让你咳起来，正合肺炎的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pneuma（气息、风）→ pneumon（肺，即「呼吸的器官」）→ pneumonia（肺病）→ 拉丁语 pneumonia → 英语 pneumonia，核心义「肺里积了水、气换不动」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a diseased lung, narrows to the acute infection a patient feels, then to the infected patch on an image, to the mild walking form, and finally to the last illness of the very old.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指有病的肺，随后收窄为患者能感到的急性感染，再指影像上那片感染灶，又指症状轻微的「可行走」型，最后指高龄者临终时的那场病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air sacs filled with fluid, each breath bubbling through wet cotton.
core.cn: 核心意象：肺泡里积满液体，每次呼吸都像隔着湿棉花冒泡。

branches.en: A diseased lung is the oldest medical sense of the word.
branches.cn: 「有病的肺」是这个词最古老的医学义项。

branches.en: The acute infection is what a patient feels as fever and cough.
branches.cn: 急性感染是患者感到的发烧与咳嗽。

branches.en: One infected lobe is the same disease seen on an image.
branches.cn: 单个受感染的肺叶，是同一疾病在影像上的样子。

branches.en: The walking form is the mild end of the same infection.
branches.cn: 「可行走」型是同一感染中较轻的一端。

branches.en: General lung inflammation and the last illness of the aged share one word.
branches.cn: 「肺的炎症」与「老人临终的那场病」共用一个词。

intro.en: Pneumonia joins Greek pneumon, the lung, to the noun ending -ia; English then built pneumonic, pneumonitis and bronchopneumonia on the same stem.
intro.cn: pneumonia 由希腊语 pneumon（肺）加名词词尾 -ia 构成；英语又用同一个词干造出 pneumonic、pneumonitis 与 bronchopneumonia。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer keeps Greek pneumonia and supplies pulmo, the lung, and spirare, to breathe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层保留了希腊语的 pneumonia，并提供 pulmo（肺）与 spirare（呼吸）。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pulmo 生出 pulmonary 与 pulmonology。
spirare 生出 respire 与 inspiration。

definition_zh: 要点；得分；地点；小数点；指向
definition_en: the main idea of what someone says; a unit of score; an exact place or moment; the dot in a decimal number; also to aim or show direction
core_image: 一根手指伸出去停在半空，所有人的视线顺着这条线落到墙上同一个位置
scene: 会议室里的讨论拖了很久，白板上写满潦草的字，有人忽然把笔尖按在其中一个词上。She tapped the board and made her point in one short sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 point 指「要点」（第 1 个义项：说话人最想让人记住的那一点）；句意为她敲了敲白板，用一句短话把自己的要点说清楚。图中可辨识物件：写满字的白板、按在词上的笔尖、几张转过来的脸。

derivatives.zh: 由 point 加 -ed 构成，义为「尖的；有针对性的」
由 point 加 -er 构成，义为「指示棒；提示；指针」
由 point 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无意义的；没有尖头的」
与 point 同出拉丁语 punctum，义为「准时的」，原指恰好落在某一刻

senses.title: The main idea in what is said
senses.definition: the central idea that a speaker or writer wants to be understood and remembered
senses.definitionCN: 说话人或作者最想让人理解并记住的那个中心意思
senses.example: Her point was that the plan costs far too much.
senses.exampleCN: 她的要点是这个方案花费太高。
senses.why: Latin punctum named the small mark left by a prick, and a mark is exactly what you put beside the one thing that must not be missed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 punctum 指被刺出的小痕，而人们正是用记号标出那件绝不能漏掉的事。

senses.title: A unit of score in a game or test
senses.definition: one of the units by which a game, a contest or an examination is measured
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一场比赛、一次竞赛或一场考试的计量单位
senses.example: He won the final point with a serve down the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记压边线的发球拿下了最后一分。
senses.why: A score was once kept by making a small mark for each success, so the mark itself became the unit of winning.
senses.whyCN: 过去记分就是每得一分画一个小记号，于是记号本身成了计量的单位。

senses.title: A particular place or moment
senses.definition: an exact spot on a map, a body or a scale, or a particular moment in time
senses.definitionCN: 地图、身体或刻度上确切的一处，或时间上特定的某一刻
senses.example: We met at the point where the two roads meet.
senses.exampleCN: 我们约在两条路交汇的那一点见面。
senses.why: A dot fixes a position and nothing else, which is why the same noun can pin down a place on a map and a moment on a timeline.
senses.whyCN: 一个点只固定位置，别的什么也不带，所以同一个名词既能标定地图上的一处，也能标定时间轴上的一刻。

senses.title: The dot in a decimal number
senses.definition: the mark that separates the whole part of a number from its fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把一个数的整数部分与小数部分分开的记号
senses.example: The reading was three point seven metres.
senses.exampleCN: 读数是三点七米。
senses.why: Because the dot is literally a small prick on the page, the mark that splits a decimal simply inherited the name of the mark itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为那个点字面上就是纸上的一个小刺痕，分开整数与小数的记号便直接继承了「记号」这个名字。

senses.title: To aim or show direction
senses.definition: to turn a finger or an object towards something, or to show what is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 把手指或物体转向某处，或显示出什么是真的、什么是可能发生的
senses.example: The arrow points north along the coastal path.
senses.exampleCN: 箭头指向沿海小路的北面。
senses.why: A pointed finger and a written dot do the same job, both singling out one thing among many, so the noun turned into a verb of directing attention.
senses.whyCN: 伸出的手指与纸上的点做的是同一件事，都是在众多事物里单单挑出一个，于是名词转成了引导注意的动词。

intro.en: Point comes from a Latin word for a prick and the mark it leaves; the dot is the oldest picture behind the score, the argument and the pointing finger.
intro.cn: point 出自拉丁语中表示「刺」的词以及刺出的痕迹；那个小点，就是得分、论点与指路手指背后最古老的画面。

items.en: The verb pungere meant to prick or pierce, the action of a sharp tip against a surface.
items.cn: 动词 pungere 意为刺、扎，是尖锐之物抵住表面的动作。

items.en: Its neuter past participle punctum named the tiny mark or hole left behind, and so came to mean a dot.
items.cn: 它的中性过去分词 punctum 指留下的细微痕迹或小孔，于是有了「点」的意思。

items.en: Old French point carried the dot, but also a stitch, a moment and a item in an argument.
items.cn: 古法语 point 既保留「点」，也指针脚、某一刻以及论述中的一项。

items.en: English took point first for a dot or a sharp end, then for a mark in a game and the chief item of a speech.
items.cn: 英语先以 point 指点状物或尖端，随后指比赛中的记号与讲话里的主要一项。

items.en: Modern English adds the decimal point, the pointing gesture, point of view, and dozens of fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上小数点、指点的动作、point of view 以及大量固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group stays on the Latin prick and its mark; the near-meaning group gathers the dot, the score, the stage and the act of aiming.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语「刺」及其痕迹展开；近义组收点、得分、阶段与瞄准这些意思。

entries.definition: Having a sharp end, or clearly aimed at one person.
entries.definitionCN: 有尖端的；明显针对某一个人的。

entries.definition: A stick, cursor or hint that shows where to look.
entries.definitionCN: 指示棒、光标或提示。

entries.definition: Having no purpose or result at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有目的或结果的。

entries.definition: Arriving exactly at the agreed time.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好在约定时刻到达的。

entries.definition: The marks such as commas and full stops used in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 书写中使用的逗号、句号等标记。

entries.definition: A small round mark.
entries.definitionCN: 小而圆的点。

entries.definition: The number of points won in a game.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛中赢得的分数。

entries.definition: A particular point in a process or development.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或发展中的某一阶段。

entries.definition: To point or direct something at a target.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物对准目标。

normalIntro.en: Everything here grows from one tiny mark made by a sharp tip, and that mark still explains the score, the argument and the finger.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的一切都长自尖端留下的一个小记号，而这个记号至今能解释得分、论点与手指。

normal.en: Pungere means to prick, and punctum is the mark a prick leaves, so every sense starts from a tiny mark.
normal.cn: pungere 意为刺，punctum 是刺出的小痕，所以每个义项都从这一个小记号出发。

normal.en: To point at something is to put an invisible dot on it, which is why the noun became a verb.
normal.cn: 指着某物，等于在它上面放一个看不见的点，名词就这样变成了动词。

normal.en: A point in a game was once a tally mark, so the score and the dot are the same mark seen twice.
normal.cn: 比赛中的一分原本就是一个记数记号，所以得分与点其实是同一个记号的两次现身。

normal.en: The decimal point is a real dot on the page, and it is the oldest physical sense surviving almost unchanged.
normal.cn: 小数点是纸上真实的一点，也是几乎原封不动留存下来的最古老的实指义。

normal.en: Pointless adds -less, without a point, and the metaphor is still visible: something with nothing to aim at.
normal.cn: pointless 加 -less，意为「没有点」，比喻仍然看得见：没有可瞄准之处。

abstract.en: The same mark that measures a game also marks the one sentence worth remembering, which says how close play and argument are.
abstract.cn: 衡量比赛的记号也被用来标出那句值得记住的话，可见游戏与论辩有多近。

abstract.en: A point is a decision about where to stop: a dot chooses a place on a map the way a conclusion chooses a place in an argument.
abstract.cn: 一个点就是决定在哪里停下：圆点在地图上选定一处，正如结论在论述中选定一处。

abstract.en: When someone says you have missed the point, the image is still spatial, as if the meaning had a location you walked past.
abstract.cn: 当有人说你错过了要点，这个说法仍是空间性的，仿佛意义有一个你走过了的位置。

examples.en: Let me make one point before we vote.
examples.cn: 在投票之前，请让我说明一点。

examples.en: She has already scored twenty points this season.
examples.cn: 这个赛季她已经得了二十分。

examples.en: From this point the road climbs steeply.
examples.cn: 从这里开始，路陡然向上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖因特」——手指一剖，直直对着那一个点，不偏不倚。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ 过去分词 punctum（刺出的点、记号）→ 古法语 point → 英语 point。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mark made by a sharp tip; from it come the idea worth marking, the tally of a game, a fixed spot in space or time, the decimal dot and the act of aiming.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是尖端留下的一个记号；由此生出值得标记的意思、比赛的记数、时空中的定点、小数点以及瞄准的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger held out and stopped in mid-air, every eye in the room following the line to one spot on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指伸出后停在半空，满屋的视线都顺着这条线落在墙上同一处。

branches.en: a sentence that makes a long meeting fall into place
branches.cn: 一句话让冗长的会议落到实处

branches.en: a serve landing just inside the line
branches.cn: 一记刚好落在边线内的发球

branches.en: two roads meeting at one exact spot
branches.cn: 两条路交于确切的一点

branches.en: a dot splitting a number in two
branches.cn: 一个点把数字分成两半

branches.en: a finger and a sentence both singling out one thing
branches.cn: 手指与句子都在挑出同一件事

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricking, its participle turned noun, and a French borrowing together supply the whole family of marks and aims.
intro.cn: 一个表示刺的拉丁动词、由分词转成的名词，加上一次法语借入，共同支撑起这整族关于记号与瞄准的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 毒药；毒物；下毒；污染；毒害
definition_en: a substance that harms or kills when it enters the body; also to put such a substance into something, to pollute a natural resource, or to corrupt a mind or a relationship
core_image: 一只没有标签的深色小瓶放在高高的架子上，瓶口沾着干涸的痕迹，旁边的人伸手前先停了一下
scene: 厨房角落的柜子上放着一只没有标签的旧瓶子，孩子踮脚要去够，母亲一把把他拉开。The faded label warned that the bottle contained a deadly poison.
sceneCN: 这里 poison 指「毒药、毒物」（第 1 个义项：进入身体后致病或致死的东西）；句意为褪色的标签警告说，这瓶里装着致命的毒药。图中可辨识物件：旧瓶子、模糊的标签、踮脚的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由 poison 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「有毒的；极有害的」
由 poison 加 -ing 构成，义为「下毒；中毒」
由 poison 加 -er 构成，义为「下毒者」
由 poisonous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有毒地；恶意地」

senses.title: A substance that harms or kills
senses.definition: a substance that causes illness or death when swallowed, breathed in or absorbed through the skin
senses.definitionCN: 吞下、吸入或经皮肤吸收后引起疾病或死亡的物质
senses.example: Rat poison must be kept away from children and pets.
senses.exampleCN: 灭鼠毒药必须放在儿童和宠物够不到的地方。
senses.why: Latin potio meant simply a drink, and because a prepared draught could heal or kill, the word slid towards the deadly kind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 potio 本只指「一饮」，而调好的药水既能治病也能致命，词义便滑向致命的那一类。

senses.title: To put poison into something
senses.definition: to add poison to food, drink or another substance, or to kill a person or animal that way
senses.definitionCN: 把毒物放进食物、饮料或其他物质里，或用这种方式杀死人或动物
senses.example: Someone had poisoned the well during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 有人夜里在水井里下了毒。
senses.why: Once the noun named the substance, plain conversion let English say what a person does with it, with no suffix added at all.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指认了这种物质，英语不必加任何后缀，直接转作动词就能说人拿它去做什么。

senses.title: To pollute a natural resource
senses.definition: to make water, air, soil or food harmful by adding a dangerous substance
senses.definitionCN: 通过加入危险物质使水、空气、土壤或食物变得有害
senses.example: Waste from the factory had poisoned the river for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的废料把这条河污染了好几英里。
senses.why: Poison need not be administered on purpose; anything that makes a shared resource unsafe behaves like poison, so the verb widens to pollution.
senses.whyCN: 毒物不必被人有意投入；任何让公共资源变得不安全的东西都起着毒物的作用，于是动词扩展到污染。

senses.title: To corrupt a mind or a relationship
senses.definition: to spoil someone's mind, trust or a relationship so that it stops working well
senses.definitionCN: 败坏某人的心智、信任或一段关系，使其不再正常运转
senses.example: Years of rumour had poisoned the friendship between the two families.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的流言败坏了这两家人之间的友谊。
senses.why: The body is not the only thing that can be poisoned: a mind fed on lies or a bond fed on suspicion shows the same damage, so the word moves into feeling.
senses.whyCN: 能被毒害的不只是身体：被谎言喂养的心智、被猜疑喂养的关系会显出同样的损伤，于是这个词进入情感领域。

intro.en: Poison began as a Latin word for a drink, narrowed into the deadly draught, and then widened again to pollution and to corrupted minds.
intro.cn: poison 最初是拉丁语中表示「饮料」的词，先收窄为致命的一剂，后来又扩展到污染与败坏的心智。

items.en: The verb potare meant to drink, and it named the ordinary act of taking liquid.
items.cn: 动词 potare 意为喝，指的是喝下液体的平常动作。

items.en: The noun potio was a drink or a draught, including a prepared potion that might cure or harm.
items.cn: 名词 potio 指饮料或一剂，也包括调好的、可能治病也可能伤人的药水。

items.en: Old French reshaped potio into poison, keeping the sense of a prepared drink and adding the sense of a deadly one.
items.cn: 古法语把 potio 改造成 poison，既保留「调制好的饮品」义，又添上「致命的一剂」义。

items.en: Middle English used poison for any harmful substance and, by conversion, for the act of administering it.
items.cn: 中古英语用 poison 指任何有害物质，并通过词性转换指投入这种物质的行为。

items.en: Modern English widened it to polluted rivers and poisoned minds, and kept compounds such as poison gas and food poisoning.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到被污染的河流与被毒害的心智，并保留 poison gas、food poisoning 这类复合说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the poison family and one close cousin from the same drink word; the near-meaning group gathers animal and chemical terms for harmful substances.
note.cn: 形近组收 poison 词族，以及同出「饮料」一词的近亲；近义组收指有害物质的动物性与化学性词语。

entries.definition: Full of poison, or extremely harmful in effect.
entries.definitionCN: 充满毒物的；效果极有害的。

entries.definition: The act of giving poison, or the illness that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 下毒的行为，或随后出现的中毒。

entries.definition: A person who puts poison into something.
entries.definitionCN: 往东西里下毒的人。

entries.definition: A liquid credited with magical or medical power, from the same drink word.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为有魔力或疗效的液体，与 poison 同出「饮料」一词。

entries.definition: The poison produced by a snake, spider or similar animal.
entries.definitionCN: 蛇、蜘蛛等动物分泌的毒液。

entries.definition: A poison produced by a living cell or organism.
entries.definitionCN: 由活细胞或生物体产生的毒素。

entries.definition: To make something dirty or unsafe by adding a harmful substance.
entries.definitionCN: 通过加入有害物质使某物变脏或不安全。

entries.definition: To make air, water or land harmful to use.
entries.definitionCN: 使空气、水或土地变得有害而不可用。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with something you swallow, and every later sense keeps that image of a substance entering where it should not.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一件被吞下的东西开始，此后每个义项都保留着「有东西进入本不该进入之处」的画面。

normal.en: Potare means to drink and potio is a draught, so poison began as something you swallow rather than something that burns.
normal.cn: potare 意为喝，potio 是一剂饮品，所以 poison 最初是被吞下的东西，而不是灼人的东西。

normal.en: French reshaped potio into poison while keeping the sense of a prepared drink, which is why the word still sounds medicinal.
normal.cn: 法语把 potio 改成 poison，同时保留「调制好的一剂」的意思，所以这个词至今带着药水味。

normal.en: Poison is noun and verb in one shape, a plain English conversion with no ending added.
normal.cn: poison 名词与动词同形，是英语里不加词尾的朴素转换。

normal.en: Poisonous adds -ous, full of, and works as the adjective; poisoning adds -ing and names the act or the resulting illness.
normal.cn: poisonous 加 -ous，意为「充满……的」，作形容词；poisoning 加 -ing，指下毒行为或由此引起的中毒。

normal.en: Modern English keeps compounds such as poison gas and food poisoning, where the old noun does the work of an adjective.
normal.cn: 现代英语保留 poison gas 与 food poisoning 这类复合词，旧的名称在里面起着形容词的作用。

abstract.en: A word for a drink becoming a word for death is a reminder that the same prepared cup can go either way.
abstract.cn: 一个表示饮料的词变成表示死亡的词，提醒人：同样一只调好的杯子可以走向两个方向。

abstract.en: The move from a bottle to a river to a friendship shows English trusting one image to cover very different kinds of harm.
abstract.cn: 从瓶子到河流再到友情，可见英语放心地用同一幅画面覆盖差别极大的伤害。

abstract.en: To speak of poisoned trust is to treat a feeling as a body with its own circulation, which can be tainted from inside.
abstract.cn: 说信任被毒害，就是把一种感受当成有自身循环的身体，可以从内部被污染。

examples.en: The berries look harmless but contain a strong poison.
examples.cn: 这些浆果看着无害，却含有强烈的毒素。

examples.en: Industrial waste has poisoned the groundwater.
examples.cn: 工业废料已经污染了地下水。

examples.en: Resentment had slowly poisoned their partnership.
examples.cn: 怨恨慢慢败坏了他们的合作关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼伊怎」——往水里泼一勺不明的东西，谁喝了都说不清会怎样。

root: 拉丁语 potare（喝）→ potio（一饮、药水）→ 古法语 poison（饮品；毒药）→ 英语 poison；本义与「喝下的一剂」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a harmful draught; the senses divide into the substance itself, the act of administering it, the pollution of a shared resource, and the corruption of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一剂有害的饮物；义项分为物质本身、投入的动作、对公共资源的污染，以及对情感的败坏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark unlabelled bottle on a high shelf, a dried stain at its lip, and a hand that stops before reaching for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：高架上一只没有标签的深色瓶子，瓶口留着干涸的痕迹，一只手伸到一半停住了。

branches.en: a dark bottle kept on the top shelf
branches.cn: 放在最高一层架子上的深色瓶子

branches.en: a well made unsafe during the night
branches.cn: 夜里被人做了手脚的水井

branches.en: a river carrying waste past the fields
branches.cn: 带着废物流过田地的河

branches.en: a friendship soured by years of rumour
branches.cn: 被多年流言泡坏的友情

branches.en: one word for a swallowed substance and a swallowed lie
branches.cn: 同一个词既指吞下的东西，也指吞下的谎言

intro.en: A Latin verb of drinking and its noun of a draught supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adjective, the act and the person from it.
intro.cn: 一个表示喝的拉丁动词和它表示「一剂」的名词提供词干，英语后缀再由此造出形容词、行为与施事者。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 有毒的；含毒的；有毒腺的；吃了会中毒的；恶毒的
definition_en: containing or producing a poison that can harm or kill, and figuratively full of bitterness and ill will
core_image: 贴着骷髅标签的棕色瓶子，盖子一开就冒出白气
scene: 实验室的通风柜前，助手把护目镜又压紧了一点，才去拧那只棕色瓶子的盖子。The label warns that the fumes are poisonous if the bottle is left open.
sceneCN: 这里是「含有毒物的、有毒的」（第 1 个义项：物质本身含毒）；句意为标签警告说，瓶子敞着放，里面冒出的气体就是有毒的。画面里有通风柜、护目镜和一只棕色试剂瓶。

pos.zh: 有毒的；含毒的；有毒腺的；恶毒的

derivatives.zh: 由 poisonous 去掉形容词后缀 -ous 得到的名词，义为「毒药；毒物」
与名词同形的动词，义为「下毒；毒害」
由 poison 加 -ing 构成，义为「下毒；中毒」
由 poisonous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有毒地；恶毒地」

senses.title: Containing a substance that harms or kills
senses.definition: containing or giving off a poison that can damage the body or cause death
senses.definitionCN: 含有或散发出能损害身体、甚至致死的毒物
senses.example: The tank was sealed because the gas inside was poisonous.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子被密封起来，因为里面的气体有毒。
senses.why: The suffix -ous says that something is full of what the noun names, so the adjective first describes what the material contains rather than whom it hurts.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 表示「充满名词所指之物」，所以这个形容词先说的是材料里含有什么，而不是它伤了谁。

senses.title: Producing venom and able to inject it
senses.titleCN: 有毒腺的；会咬人放毒的
senses.definition: used of an animal that makes venom in its body and can pass it on by biting or stinging
senses.definitionCN: 用于体内制造毒液、并能通过咬或蜇把毒液注入对方身体的动物
senses.example: Only a few of the snakes in this region are poisonous.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带只有少数几种蛇是有毒的。
senses.why: English uses one adjective for a swallowed poison and for injected venom, because in both cases a living body is carrying a dose of harm inside it.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个形容词覆盖吞下去的毒和被注入的毒液，因为两种情形都是一个活体身上带着一份会伤人的剂量。

senses.title: Unsafe to eat
senses.definition: used of food, berries or mushrooms that make a person ill or kill them once swallowed
senses.definitionCN: 用于一旦吃下就会让人生病或致命的食物、浆果与蘑菇
senses.example: She threw the berries away because some of them were poisonous.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那些浆果扔了，因为其中有些是有毒的。
senses.why: Once the adjective describes what a thing contains rather than how it attacks, it settles easily on food, where the danger appears only after swallowing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个形容词说的是「东西里含有什么」而不是「它怎么攻击」，它就很容易落到食物上，因为那里的危险要等吞下去之后才出现。

senses.title: Full of bitterness and ill will
senses.definition: full of hatred or malice, said of remarks, feelings or the mood of a place
senses.definitionCN: 充满憎恨或恶意，用于言语、情绪或一个地方的氛围
senses.example: The meeting turned poisonous once the two managers began to trade blame.
senses.exampleCN: 两位经理一开始互相推卸责任，会议的气氛就变得充满敌意。
senses.why: Poison works unseen and spreads through whatever carries it, so the same word describes words or moods that infect everyone who breathes them in.
senses.whyCN: 毒物看不见，却会顺着载着它的东西扩散，于是同一个词也形容话语或情绪，谁吸进去谁就被感染。

intro.en: Poisonous is the noun poison with the adjective suffix -ous, and poison itself goes back to a Latin word for a drink that could heal or kill.
intro.cn: poisonous 是名词 poison 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成的，而 poison 本身源自一个既可治病也可致命的拉丁语「饮剂」词。

items.en: Potio meant a drink, especially a measured draught, and the same word could name a healing cup or a harmful one.
items.cn: potio 意为「饮料」，尤指按量配好的一剂，同一个词既能指治病的药饮，也能指害人的毒饮。

items.en: The verb potare meant to drink, and it stands behind the drink words of this family, including English potable.
items.cn: 动词 potare 意为「喝」，这一族与饮用有关的词都由它而来，英语的 potable 也在其中。

items.en: Old French poison still meant a drink or potion, but in medieval use it was most often a harmful draught handed to a victim.
items.cn: 古法语 poison 仍指饮料或药剂，但在中世纪的用法里，它多半指递给受害者的一杯毒饮。

items.en: Middle English borrowed poison as a noun for a deadly substance, and English then added -ous to name the quality of containing it.
items.cn: 中古英语把 poison 借作名词，指致命的物质；英语随后加 -ous，用来指「含有这种物质」的性质。

items.en: Modern English keeps both noun and adjective and widens the adjective to venomous animals, spoiled food and bitter speech.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留名词与形容词，并把形容词扩展到有毒的动物、变质的食物和刻薄的言辞。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the drink words of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things that harm the body.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族里与「饮剂」有关的词；近义组收表示「伤害身体」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun the adjective is built on: a substance that harms or kills.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词所由来的名词：能伤害或杀死人的物质。

entries.definition: A drink with supposed magical or medicinal power, from the Latin word for a draught.
entries.definitionCN: 据称有魔力或药效的饮剂，源自拉丁语中表示「一饮」的词。

entries.definition: Safe or fit to drink, built on the Latin verb meaning to drink.
entries.definitionCN: 可以安全饮用的，建立在拉丁语「喝」这一动词上。

entries.definition: The act of giving poison, or the illness that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 下毒的行为，或随之而来的中毒。

entries.definition: Poisonous in a scientific or medical register, often of chemicals.
entries.definitionCN: 科学或医学语境里的「有毒」，多指化学品。

entries.definition: Producing venom and injecting it by bite or sting.
entries.definitionCN: 产生毒液并通过咬或蜇注入的。

entries.definition: Harmful to health, especially of fumes or smells.
entries.definitionCN: 有害健康的，多指气体或气味。

entries.definition: Able to cause damage of any kind, weaker than poisonous.
entries.definitionCN: 能造成任何伤害的，语气比 poisonous 轻。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is a Latin word for a draught wearing the suffix of fullness, and both halves still show in how it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁语「一饮」披上表示「充满」的后缀，两半至今都能从用法里看出来。

normal.en: -ous means full of, so poisonous is literally full of poison and describes what a thing carries.
normal.cn: -ous 表示「充满」，所以 poisonous 字面就是「充满毒」，说的是东西里装着什么。

normal.en: Poison and potion share the Latin word for a drink, which is why the old image of poison is a cup, not a wound.
normal.cn: poison 与 potion 共用拉丁语中「饮料」这个词，所以毒最古老的画面是一只杯子，而不是一道伤口。

normal.en: A poisonous snake carries venom in its body, while poisonous gas fills a room; English lets one adjective cover both.
normal.cn: poisonous snake 把毒液带在身上，poisonous gas 把毒气充满房间，英语让一个形容词同时管这两种情形。

normal.en: Poisoning is the noun for the event, and poisonously is the adverb for the manner, so the family covers thing, act and style.
normal.cn: poisoning 是表示事件的名词，poisonously 是表示方式副词，这一族词因此覆盖了物、事与姿态。

normal.en: Potable comes from the same verb for drinking but means safe to drink, showing that relatives can take opposite sides.
normal.cn: potable 出自同一个「喝」的动词，意思却是「能安全饮用」，可见同族词可以站到相反的一边。

abstract.en: A word that starts as a drink reminds us that harm often arrives in something we are glad to receive.
abstract.cn: 一个从「饮料」起步的词提醒人：伤害常常藏在一样我们乐于接受的东西里。

abstract.en: Because poison spreads through a carrier, the same adjective can describe air, a snake and a sentence.
abstract.cn: 因为毒要靠载体扩散，同一个形容词才能既形容空气，又形容蛇，还形容一句话。

abstract.en: The step from substance to mood is short: what cannot be seen is what most easily fills a room.
abstract.cn: 从物质到情绪的跨度很短：看不见的东西，最容易充满一个房间。

examples.en: The tank was sealed because the gas inside was poisonous.
examples.cn: 罐子被密封起来，因为里面的气体有毒。

examples.en: She threw the berries away because some of them were poisonous.
examples.cn: 她把那些浆果扔了，因为其中有些是有毒的。

examples.en: A poisonous silence filled the room after his remark.
examples.cn: 他那一句话之后，房间里弥漫着敌意的沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼伊怎死」——毒液泼到人身上，沾上就难逃一死，这就是 poisonous 的有毒。

root: 拉丁语 potio（饮剂）与 potare（喝）经古法语 poison 进入英语，先指饮下的一剂，后专指毒物；再加 -ous 构成 poisonous。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a thing that carries harm inside it; from that come the venomous animal, the dangerous food, and finally the bitter mood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「里面带着伤害的东西」；由此分出带毒液的动物、危险的食物，最后是刻薄的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown bottle with a skull label, white vapour rising as the cap comes off.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着骷髅标签的棕色瓶子，盖子一开就冒出白气。

branches.en: a sealed jar marked with a skull
branches.cn: 贴着骷髅标记的密封罐

branches.en: a snake coiled with its head raised
branches.cn: 盘起身子昂起头的蛇

branches.en: a child pulled back from wild berries
branches.cn: 孩子被拉回来，没去摘野果

branches.en: a room going quiet after a cruel remark
branches.cn: 一句刻薄话之后安静下来的房间

branches.en: a warning sign nailed beside a well
branches.cn: 钉在水井旁的警示牌

intro.en: A Latin word for a drink, its verb, and one English suffix of fullness hold this word together, and the family splits into the substance, the act and the manner.
intro.cn: 一个表示「饮剂」的拉丁名词、它的动词，加上一个表示「充满」的英语后缀，撑起这个词；这一族再分出物质、行为与方式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 政治的；政党的；政治性的；涉及权力关系的；关心并参与政治的
definition_en: relating to government, parties or public power, and also used of anything shaped by the struggle for influence
core_image: 竞选办公室的墙上一层层贴着海报，志愿者守着电话名单逐个催票
scene: 选举前夜，竞选办公室的墙上贴满海报，志愿者守着电话名单逐个催票。The rally was a political event from the first speech to the last handshake.
sceneCN: 这里指「与政党及选举有关的」，对应第 2 个义项：属于党派竞争与投票活动范畴的；句意为这场造势集会从第一场演讲到最后一次握手都是政治活动。画面要点：海报墙、电话名单、成排折叠椅；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 政治的；与政府、政党或公共权力有关的
政治性的；出于权力考量的（含贬义时指为利益而非为原则）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 在政治方面；从政治角度
使政治化；使带上党派色彩
政治化
使去政治化；把争议移出政治领域
不问政治的；与政治无关的

senses.title: Relating to government and public affairs
senses.titleCN: 与政府及公共事务有关
senses.definition: concerned with the state, its institutions and the making of public decisions
senses.definitionCN: 涉及国家、其机构以及公共决定的作出
senses.example: The constitution sets the political institutions of the country.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法确立了这个国家的政治机构。
senses.why: the Greek adjective meant 'of citizens, civic', so political first described what belongs to the organised community.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊形容词意为「公民的、城邦的」，因此 political 最初描述属于有组织共同体的事物。

senses.title: Relating to parties and elections
senses.definition: belonging to the competition of parties, campaigns and votes
senses.definitionCN: 属于政党竞争、竞选活动与投票的范畴
senses.example: The rally was a political event from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这场集会从头到尾都是政治活动。
senses.why: when civic business organised itself into parties, the adjective followed the contest rather than the institution.
senses.whyCN: 当城邦事务组织成党派之后，这个形容词就跟着竞争走，而不只指机构。

senses.title: Moved by power rather than by merit
senses.titleCN: 出于权力考量而非事理本身
senses.definition: describing a choice made to protect influence or advantage rather than because it is right or efficient
senses.definitionCN: 形容某项选择是为保住影响力或优势而作，而非因为它正确或高效
senses.example: The appointment was political, not technical.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任命是政治性的，不是技术性的。
senses.why: once the adjective can mean 'of the contest', it can also mean 'shaped by the contest', and that reading carries the criticism.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个形容词能表示「属于竞争」，也就能表示「被竞争左右」，后一种读法自带批评意味。

senses.title: Sensitive or contested in public terms
senses.titleCN: 在公共层面敏感、容易引发争执
senses.definition: describing a topic that arouses strong public disagreement and is therefore hard to handle openly
senses.definitionCN: 形容会激起强烈公共分歧、因而难以公开处理的话题
senses.example: Water rights are a political subject in every dry province.
senses.exampleCN: 在每个干旱省份，水权都是敏感的政治话题。
senses.why: topics become political when they enter the space where groups must take sides, so the adjective marks that entry.
senses.whyCN: 话题一旦进入群体必须站队的那个空间，就变得政治化，这个形容词标记的正是这一进入。

senses.title: Power relations inside an organization
senses.definition: describing the informal side of an institution where influence, alliance and status are at stake
senses.definitionCN: 形容机构中影响力、结盟与地位暗中较劲的那一面
senses.example: A political reading of the memo explained why the plan died.
senses.exampleCN: 从权力关系的角度读这份备忘录，就能解释这个方案为何夭折。
senses.why: the pattern of alliance and rivalry repeats in firms and faculties, so the adjective travels wherever scarce goods are allocated.
senses.whyCN: 结盟与对立的格局在企业与院系里都会重演，因此只要稀缺之物需要分配，这个形容词就会跟过去。

senses.title: Engaged or aware as a person
senses.titleCN: 形容关心并参与政治的人
senses.definition: describing a person who follows public affairs and acts on them, as in a very political family
senses.definitionCN: 形容关注公共事务并付诸行动的人，如一个政治气氛浓厚的家庭
senses.example: She came from a political family and knew the ward maps by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 她出身于政治家庭，把选区地图记得滚瓜烂熟。
senses.why: the adjective applies to people as well as things, and then it means absorbed in the activity rather than belonging to it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可用于人，此时指沉浸在政治活动中，而不是属于某个机构。

senses.title: Belonging to the state sphere
senses.titleCN: 属于国家领域而非民间或宗教领域
senses.definition: marking the boundary between matters of the state and matters of faith, market or private life
senses.definitionCN: 标出国家事务与信仰、市场或私人生活之间的界线
senses.example: The dispute was religious in form and political in effect.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端形式上属宗教，实际效果上属政治。
senses.why: a society divides its spheres, and the adjective names the one that ends in enforceable collective decisions.
senses.whyCN: 社会把领域划分开来，这个形容词所指的正是最终以可强制执行的集体决定收尾的那一个领域。

senses.title: Abstract: concerning who decides collectively
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：关乎集体由谁决定
senses.definition: in general use, touching on the question of who has the right to make a binding choice for a group
senses.definitionCN: 泛指触及「谁有权为一个群体作出有约束力的选择」这一问题
senses.example: Even the choice of a chairman became political.
senses.exampleCN: 连选谁当主席都变成了政治问题。
senses.why: the abstract sense reduces the word to one question, namely who may decide for the group.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把这个词压缩成一个问题，即为群体作决定的权利归谁。

intro.en: Political is the English form of a Greek adjective meaning 'of citizens', built on the word for a city-state. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: political 是希腊语中意为「公民的」这一形容词在英语里的形式，其词根是表示城邦的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis named a city-state and its citizen body; its deeper origin is not settled, and a pre-Greek source is a hypothesis rather than an established fact.
items.cn: polis 指城邦及其公民总体；它更深的来源未有定论，前希腊语来源只是假说，并非已确认的事实。

items.en: Politikos meant 'of a citizen, civic, fit for governing', and it described affairs that concerned the community rather than the household.
items.cn: politikos 意为「公民的、城邦的、适于治理的」，描述与共同体相关、而非与家户相关的事务。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective as politicus and used it for civil and state affairs, especially in translations of Greek political works.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个形容词借作 politicus，用于民政与国家事务，尤其在翻译希腊政治著作时使用。

items.en: Middle French politique took the word into English in the fifteenth century, first as a noun for the study of the state and soon after as an adjective.
items.cn: 中古法语 politique 在十五世纪把这个词带入英语，先作名词指对国家的研究，随后不久用作形容词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective was extended to party competition and then to any sphere where influence is contested, including offices and universities.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词先扩用到党派竞争，再扩用到任何影响力受争夺的领域，包括办公室与大学。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same civic stem that are easily mistaken for this adjective; group two holds adjectives that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「城邦」词干、容易被误当作本词的词；第二组是含义部分重叠的形容词。

entries.definition: A shorter adjective meaning shrewd and tactful; a politic move is a wise one, not necessarily a governmental one.
entries.definitionCN: 更短的同源形容词，意为精明得体的；得体的举动是明智之举，未必与国家有关。

entries.definition: The adverb form, used for the standpoint or the consequences in power terms, as in politically impossible.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，用于表示政治角度或权力层面的后果，如政治上不可行。

entries.definition: Built with a negative prefix, it means indifferent to or outside politics, and is the direct opposite of one sense of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 由否定前缀构成，意为不问政治的或与政治无关的，与本词的某一义项正好相反。

entries.definition: The activity itself; the adjective describes what belongs to it or resembles it.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动本身；本词形容词则描述属于该活动或与之相似的事物。

entries.definition: Relating to government as an institution; it does not extend to party contests or office manoeuvring.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为机构的政府有关；不延伸到党派竞争或办公室权术。

entries.definition: Loyal to a party or cause; political can be neutral, while partisan always implies taking sides.
entries.definitionCN: 忠于某党或某项主张；political 可以是中性的，而 partisan 总意味着站队。

entries.definition: Relating to the duties and rights of citizens in a town; it is about membership rather than about power struggle.
entries.definitionCN: 与市民的义务和权利有关；侧重成员身份，而非权力争夺。

entries.definition: Concerning the community as a whole or open to view; it lacks the connotation of contest for authority.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及整个共同体或对外公开；不含争夺权威的意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The stem is the Greek word for a city-state, so the adjective originally means 'belonging to the citizen body'.
normal.cn: 词干是希腊语中表示城邦的词，所以这个形容词本义是「属于公民总体的」。

normal.en: The family runs political, politically, politics, politician, politicize and apolitical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治的、在政治上、政治、从政者、使政治化与不问政治的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institutional sense: political party, political system, political will, political debate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出制度义：政党、政治制度、政治意愿、政治辩论。

normal.en: Saying a decision was political is a criticism; saying a map is political is a description.
normal.cn: 说某个决定是政治性的，是批评；说某张地图是政治的，是描述。

normal.en: The pair to remember is politic for prudent and political for governmental.
normal.cn: 要记住的对照是：较短的 politic 指精明得体，political 指与国家相关。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every chair is placed to show who outranks whom.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，每把椅子的位置都在显示谁的位次更高。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn across a table, with faith on one side and enforceable rules on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上画一条线，一边是信仰，另一边是可强制执行的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall, asking not what is true but who may decide.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里举起一只手，问的不是何为真，而是谁有权决定。

examples.en: The reforms were blocked for purely political reasons.
examples.cn: 这些改革因纯粹的政治原因被搁置。

examples.en: She kept her political views out of the classroom.
examples.cn: 她不让自己的政治观点进入课堂。

examples.en: A political solution is needed before the water can be shared.
examples.cn: 在分配水源之前，需要一个政治层面的解决方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「城邦公民的」——凡涉及谁掌权、谁站队的事 → 政治的

root: political 出自希腊 politikos「公民的、城邦的」，源头为 polis「城邦」与 politēs「公民」，经拉丁 politicus 与中古法语 politique 进入英语；polis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses branch from one adjective: what belongs to the citizen body, then to parties, to power-driven choices, to sensitive topics, to office rivalries, to engaged persons, to the state sphere, and finally to any question of who decides.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个形容词分出：先属公民总体，再属党派、属出于权力的选择、属敏感话题、属办公室里的对立、属积极参与的人、属国家领域，最后属任何「谁来决定」的问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a campaign office wall layered with posters, a list of names to call.
core.cn: 核心意象：竞选办公室的墙上一层叠一层的海报，以及一列待拨的姓名。

branches.en: CIVIC BASE: the adjective first marks what belongs to the organised citizen body and its institutions.
branches.cn: 公民基础：这个形容词最初标记属于有组织公民总体及其机构的事物。

branches.en: PARTY CONTEST: once civic business is organised in parties, the adjective follows the campaign.
branches.cn: 党派竞争：城邦事务一旦组织成党派，这个形容词就跟着竞选活动走。

branches.en: MOTIVE AND SENSITIVITY: a choice can be driven by advantage, and a topic can be explosive, and one adjective covers both warnings.
branches.cn: 动机与敏感：选择可能被利益驱动，话题可能一触即发，同一个形容词兼具这两种提醒。

branches.en: SMALL SCALE AND PERSONAL: office rivalries repeat the pattern, and a person can be absorbed in it.
branches.cn: 小规模与个人：办公室的对立重演这一格局，而个人也可以沉浸其中。

branches.en: SPHERE AND QUESTION: the state sphere is marked off from faith and market, and behind it lies the bare question of who decides.
branches.cn: 领域与问题：国家领域与信仰、市场被划开，而其后正是「谁来决定」这个赤裸的问题。

intro.en: Political is a Greek adjective stem plus an English adjective ending, and the stem also builds politics, politician and policy.
intro.cn: political 是希腊形容词词干加英语形容词词尾，同一词干还造出政治、从政者与政策。

latinIntro.en: Latin politicus carried the Greek adjective into learned use, and its feminine noun politica stands behind policy and polity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 politicus 把这个希腊形容词带入学术用法，其阴性名词 politica 则是政策与政体两词的来源。

items.example: The root supplies the civic frame of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供这个词的城邦框架。

items.example: The citizen is the reference point of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 公民是这个形容词的参照点。

items.example: The suffix turns the citizen into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「公民」变成表示归属的形容词。

items.example: The adjective was used of matters of the community.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于共同体的事务。

items.example: Latin kept the adjective for civil affairs.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词保留给民政事务。

items.example: The ending makes the borrowed stem into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把借来的词干变成英语形容词。

items.example: The adverb marks the standpoint rather than the thing.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记的是角度，而非事物本身。

items.example: A budget cut politicized the whole faculty.
items.exampleCN: 一次预算削减把整个院系政治化了。

items.example: The survey was designed to look apolitical.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查被设计得看似不问政治。

definition_zh: 民意调查；投票；选举；得票数；做民意调查；获得（票数）
definition_en: a survey of people's opinions, the act or result of voting, and the verbs for surveying people or receiving a number of votes
core_image: 一只手拿笔，把人群按人头一一点过，每点一个画一道
scene: 大选前一周，街角的志愿者拿着写字板，拦住过往行人问他们会投给谁。The newspaper's latest poll shows the two candidates almost level.
sceneCN: 这里是「民意调查」（第 1 个义项：按抽样询问一批人的意见）；句意为该报最新的民调显示两名候选人几乎不相上下。画面里有街角、写字板和停下来的行人。

pos.zh: 民意调查；投票；选举；得票数
对……做民意调查；获得（票数）

derivatives.zh: 由 poll 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -ster 构成，义为「民调机构人员；民意调查员」
由 poll 加 -ing 构成，义为「投票；民意调查」
由 poll（头顶）加 -ed 构成，用于牛羊，义为「无角的」

senses.title: A survey of people's opinions
senses.definition: a survey that asks a sample of people what they think about an issue, a product or a candidate
senses.definitionCN: 就某个议题、产品或候选人询问一批抽样对象看法的调查
senses.example: An opinion poll suggested that most voters wanted the plan changed.
senses.exampleCN: 一项民意调查显示，多数选民希望这个方案作出修改。
senses.why: The word first meant a head, then a count of heads; asking people one by one repeats that counting gesture, so a survey inherits the image of ticking off person after person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指「头」，再指「按人头点数」；挨个询问正是重复那个点数的动作，于是民调继承了「一个个人画勾」的画面。

senses.title: The act of voting
senses.definition: the occasion on which people cast votes, usually in the phrase the polls or go to the polls
senses.definitionCN: 人们投下选票的场合，常见于 the polls 或 go to the polls 这样的说法
senses.example: The country went to the polls in the middle of a heat wave.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在一场热浪中举行了投票。
senses.why: Once a poll is a head count, the day when heads are counted becomes the poll itself, and voters are said to go to it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 poll 是「清点人头」，清点人头的那一天本身就成了 poll，选民也就被说成「走向」它。

senses.title: The number of votes recorded
senses.definition: the total of votes won by a candidate or party, or the record of those totals
senses.definitionCN: 某位候选人或政党赢得的票数总和，或记录这些数字的清单
senses.example: The final poll gave the mayor a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 最终得票数让市长获得了明显的多数。
senses.why: If the count produces a number, the same noun can name that number, which is how a poll comes to mean the tally a candidate watches all night.
senses.whyCN: 既然清点会得出一个数字，同一个名词就能指那个数字，于是 poll 也指候选人整夜盯着的计票结果。

senses.title: To ask people for their opinions
senses.definition: to question a group of people in order to find out what they think
senses.definitionCN: 为了解一批人的想法而向他们提问
senses.example: She polled her students about which book to read next.
senses.exampleCN: 她就下一本读什么书征求了学生们的意见。
senses.why: The noun names the survey, so the verb names the work of producing one: someone has to go out and put the questions.
senses.whyCN: 名词指调查本身，动词就指做出这项调查的过程：总得有人走出去把问题问出来。

senses.title: To receive a particular number of votes
senses.definition: to win or record a stated number or share of votes in an election
senses.definitionCN: 在选举中获得或记录下某一数字或比例的选票
senses.example: The party polled forty percent of the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 该党获得了四成选票。
senses.why: Because a poll is also the tally, the verb can be used from the other side: a candidate polls the votes that the count gives him.
senses.whyCN: 既然 poll 也指计票结果，动词就能从另一头来用：候选人 poll 到的，就是清点之后记在他名下的票。

intro.en: Poll is a Germanic word for the head that entered English from Dutch; the political senses grew out of counting people head by head, not out of Latin.
intro.cn: poll 是来自荷兰语、意为「头」的日耳曼词；它的政治义项是从「按人头点数」长出来的，与拉丁语无关。

items.en: Middle Dutch pol meant the head or the top of something, and it is generally traced to a Germanic stock rather than to Latin.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pol 意为头或某物的顶部，一般认为它上溯到日耳曼语来源，而不是拉丁语。

items.en: Middle English polle named the head, and by extension a person counted as one head in a crowd.
items.cn: 中古英语 polle 指头，引申为人群中被当作「一个头」来数的人。

items.en: A poll became a count of heads, then the record of votes at an election, and finally the place where those votes were cast.
items.cn: poll 由「清点人头」变成选举中的计票，再变成投票的场所。

items.en: Newspapers and social research gave the word its survey sense: a sample of heads asked for their opinions.
items.cn: 报纸与社会研究赋予这个词「调查」义：抽出一批人头来问他们的看法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for a survey, a vote and a tally, and uses the verb both for asking people and for the votes a candidate wins.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词的「调查、投票、计票」三义，动词则既指去问人，也指候选人赢得的票数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on this Germanic head word, with one spelling twin from a different root; the near-meaning group gathers words for surveys and voting.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在这个日耳曼「头」词上的形式，并附一个来自别的词根的拼写近邻；近义组收表示「调查」与「投票」的词。

entries.definition: A person who conducts opinion polls.
entries.definitionCN: 从事民意调查的人。

entries.definition: The act of voting, or of asking people for their views.
entries.definitionCN: 投票的行为，或向人征询意见的行为。

entries.definition: Of cattle: hornless, from the old sense of the top of the head.
entries.definitionCN: 指牛羊无角的，来自「头顶」这一旧义。

entries.definition: A long thin post; it is only spelling-alike, since it comes from a Latin word for a stake, not from the word for a head.
entries.definitionCN: 长杆；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语中表示「木桩」的词，与「头」这个词无关。

entries.definition: A study that collects answers from a group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 向一群人收集答案的研究。

entries.definition: The system or paper by which people vote.
entries.definitionCN: 投票的制度或选票本身。

entries.definition: A formal choice made in an election.
entries.definitionCN: 选举中作出的正式选择。

entries.definition: To go round an area asking for votes or opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地区走访拉票或征求意见。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one concrete act: touching a head to count it, whether in a crowd, at a ballot box or on a telephone list.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都从一个具体动作长出来：点一个头就算一个，不论是在人群里、票箱前还是电话名单上。

normal.en: Poll began as the head, and a poll of the people was a count of heads, which is why voting and surveying share the word.
normal.cn: poll 起初指「头」，a poll of the people 就是清点人头，所以投票与调查共用这个词。

normal.en: Opinion poll puts the noun after the subject it measures, and the phrase is the normal way to name a survey.
normal.cn: opinion poll 把名词放在它所测量的对象之后，是称呼民调最常用的说法。

normal.en: Go to the polls treats the word as a place or event, because the polls are where the counting happens.
normal.cn: go to the polls 把这个词当成地点或事件，因为 the polls 就是清点发生的地方。

normal.en: The verb poll takes a person or group as its object: you poll voters, students or an audience.
normal.cn: 动词 poll 以人或群体作宾语：poll voters、students、an audience。

normal.en: Pollster adds -ster, the old suffix for someone who does a thing, so the word names the person behind the numbers.
normal.cn: pollster 加了 -ster，这个古老后缀表示「做某事的人」，于是这个词指数字背后的人。

abstract.en: A word that moves from head to vote to opinion shows that public voice is always counted in bodies.
abstract.cn: 一个从「头」走到「票」再到「意见」的词说明：公共声音终究是按人头来数的。

abstract.en: The same noun can be the question, the act and the total, because a poll is a circle that closes only when the numbers come back.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既能是问题、是行为、也是总数，因为民调是一个圈，数字回来才算闭合。

abstract.en: Counting heads is a crude measure, and the word quietly admits it: what is counted is a unit, not a mind.
abstract.cn: 数人头是一种粗糙的度量，这个词也默默承认了这一点：被数的是一个单位，而不是一个头脑。

examples.en: An opinion poll suggested that most voters wanted the plan changed.
examples.cn: 一项民意调查显示，多数选民希望这个方案作出修改。

examples.en: She polled her students about which book to read next.
examples.cn: 她就下一本读什么书征求了学生们的意见。

examples.en: The party polled forty percent of the vote.
examples.cn: 该党获得了四成选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡欧」——把人头一个个数过去，数出来的是票，问出来的是民调，都是 poll。

root: 中古荷兰语 pol（头顶、头）→ 中古英语 polle（头）→ 按人头计数 → 计票与投票 → 民意调查；属日耳曼来源，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a count of heads; from it come the vote, the tally and the place of voting, and then the modern survey and its verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「清点人头」；由此分出投票、计票与投票场所，再长出当代的调查及其动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clipboard moving through a crowd, ticking one head after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写字板在人群里移动，一个头一个头地画勾。

branches.en: a clipboard stopped in front of a stranger
branches.cn: 写字板停在一个陌生人面前

branches.en: a queue outside a school hall at dawn
branches.cn: 清晨校舍外排起的队伍

branches.en: a tally sheet with numbers running down
branches.cn: 数字一路往下的计票单

branches.cn: 记者按门铃收集答案

branches.cn: 候选人午夜盯着计票

intro.en: A Germanic word for the head, an English habit of counting by heads, and two English suffixes build this family; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语的「头」词、英语「按人头计数」的习惯，加上两个英语后缀，撑起这一族；其中没有拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and has no reliable Latin cognate, so no Latin entry is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此这里不列拉丁语条目。
